Ben was very clever and brave. He went home with a smile on his face, proud of his brave act.

The rabbit told him that he'd help him find his way, so they set off together. Finally, after awhile of searching, the boy spotted his house and he ran off happily.

The rabbit stood in the field and smiled, knowing he had helped out a friend. He learned a valuable lesson that day - he should always do what he can to help someone when they're in need.

Once upon a time there was a jealous shark. He wanted to be the fastest swimmer in the sea, so he challenged a fish to a race. The fish accepted the challenge as he was very confident that he would win. But when the race started, the shark moved so quickly that he easily outswam the fish. 

The fish was embarrassed and tried to hide in the water. But the shark saw him and swam over to him. With an angry voice the Shark said: "Do you want to race again?". 

The fish replied quickly: "No! I don't want to race anymore."

The shark was so mad that he started to shake. He didn't understand why the fish didn't want to race anymore. It was so much fun! He told the fish that it was okay if he was embarrassed and he said that he would race with him again anytime. 

The shark and fish stayed friends, and they never had a race again. But they often shook fins to show they were still friends.

Ben likes to cook with his mom. He helps her to stir the soup in the big black pan. He also likes to taste the soup and say if it is good or not.

One day, mom says, "Ben, today we will make a new soup. It has carrots and potatoes and cheese. Do you want to help me?"

Ben nods and says, "Yes, mom, I want to help. I like carrots and potatoes and cheese."

Mom smiles and says, "Good, then let's start. First, we need to wash the carrots and potatoes and peel them. Can you do that?"

Ben says, "Yes, mom, I can do that." He takes a knife and a peeler and starts to peel the carrots and potatoes. He is careful not to cut himself. He puts the peels in the trash and the carrots and potatoes in a bowl.

Mom says, "Very good, Ben. You are doing a great job. Now, we need to cut the carrots and potatoes into small pieces. Can you do that?"

Ben says, "Yes, mom, I can do that." He takes the knife and starts to cut the carrots and potatoes into small pieces. He tries to make them all the same size. He puts the pieces in another bowl.

Mom says, "Wonderful, Ben. You are improving your skills. Now, we need to boil some water in the big black pan. Can you fill the pan with water and put it on the stove?"

Ben says, "Yes, mom, I can do that." He takes the big black pan and fills it with water from the faucet. He carries the pan to the stove and puts it on a burner. He turns the knob to make the fire.

Mom says, "Careful, Ben. The fire is hot. Don't touch it. Now, we need to add some salt and some cheese to the water. Can you do that?"

Ben says, "Yes, mom, I can do that." He takes a spoon and scoops some salt from a jar. He sprinkles the salt into the water. He takes a grater and grates some cheese from a block. He adds the cheese to the water.

Mom says, "Excellent, Ben. You are making a delicious soup. Now, we need to wait for the water to boil. Then, we will add the carrots and potatoes and cook them until they are soft. Can you watch the pan and tell me when it boils?"

Ben says, "Yes, mom, I can do that." He watches the pan and sees the water start to bubble. He says, "Mom, mom, the water is boiling. It is boiling."

Mom says, "Good, Ben. You are very attentive. Now, we can add the carrots and potatoes and lower the heat. We will let them cook for a while. Then, we will have a yummy soup for lunch. Do you want to taste it?"

Ben says, "Yes, mom, I want to taste it. I want to taste our soup."

Mom says, "OK, Ben. But be careful. The soup is hot. Don't burn your tongue. Here, take a spoon and try a little bit."

Ben takes a spoon and blows on the soup. He puts the spoon in his mouth and tastes the soup. He smiles and says, "Mmm, mom, the soup is good. It is very good. I like our soup."

Mom says, "I'm glad you like it, Ben. I like it too. You helped me a lot. You are a great cook. You improved our soup."

Ben says, "Thank you, mom. You are a great cook too. You taught me how to cook. I love you, mom."

Mom says, "I love you too, Ben. Now, let's enjoy our soup together."

Lily was a little girl who liked to visit her grandma's farm. She loved to see the animals, especially the sheep. They were soft and white and made funny noises.

One day, Lily saw a big sheep with a red ribbon around its neck. It was the leader of the flock and looked very proud. Lily wanted to pet it, but the sheep did not like her. It baaed loudly and ran away from her.

"Why are you so mean?" Lily asked the sheep. "I just want to be your friend."

The sheep stopped and turned to Lily. It said, "You are a human. You are not one of us. You have no wool, no horns, no hooves. You are different and strange. Go away!"

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not understand why the sheep was so rude. She looked at the other sheep, who followed the leader and ignored her. She wished she could be like them, and have their soft wool and their red ribbon.

She saw a pile of hay near the barn. She had an idea. She ran to the hay and grabbed some. She wrapped it around her head and body, trying to make herself look like a sheep. She stood on her toes and walked on the hay, pretending to have hooves. She made baaing noises and smiled.

She went back to the sheep and said, "Look at me! I am a sheep too! I have wool and hooves and a baa. Can I join you now?"

The sheep looked at Lily and laughed. They saw that she was not a real sheep, but a silly human with hay on her. They thought she was very funny and stupid. They baaed louder and louder, making fun of her.

Lily felt hurt and embarrassed. She realized that she had made a mistake. She did not want to be a sheep anymore. She wanted to be herself. She took off the hay and threw it away. She ran to her grandma, who was watching from the porch.

"Grandma, the sheep are mean to me!" Lily cried. "They don't like me because I am different. They made fun of me when I tried to be like them."

Grandma hugged Lily and said, "Don't mind them, my dear. They are just envious of you. You are a wonderful human, and you have many things that they don't. You have a beautiful face, a smart brain, a kind heart, and a big imagination. You can do anything you want, and be anything you want. You don't need to pretend to be someone else. You are perfect just the way you are."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Grandma. I love you."

"I love you too, Lily. Now, let's go and see the other animals. They are much nicer than the sheep. They will be happy to see you." Grandma said.

Lily nodded and followed Grandma. She forgot about the sheep and their red ribbon. She was happy to be herself, and to have her grandma's love.

Tom was angry too. He said, "Lily, you are a mean chef. You are not my friend either. I will go away."

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play with snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They gave him a name: Sam.

One day, the sun was very bright and warm. Anna and Ben went to see Sam, but they saw something bad. Sam was melting! His hat was falling, his scarf was loose and his carrot nose was gone. Anna and Ben were very sad and angry.

They saw a boy with a big smile and a carrot in his hand. He was the one who took Sam's nose. He said: "Ha ha, your snowman is gone. He can't talk to you anymore. He doesn't have a language."

Anna and Ben did not like the boy. He was mean and rude. They wanted to get Sam's nose back, but they did not know how. They thought hard and had an idea.

They said to the boy: "You are right, our snowman can't talk to us. But he can talk to you. He is very wise and knows many things. He can tell you a secret, if you give him his nose back."

The boy was curious and greedy. He wanted to know the secret. He gave Sam his nose back and leaned close to his ear. But Sam did not say anything. He was just a snowman.

Anna and Ben laughed and said: "The secret is: you are a fool. You should not take things that are not yours. You should be kind and share. That is what wise people do."

The boy felt ashamed and sorry. He said: "I am sorry, Anna and Ben. I was wrong and mean. Can we be friends?"

Anna and Ben smiled and said: "Yes, we can be friends. But you have to promise to be nice and good."

The boy promised and they all played together. They had fun and learned a lesson. The sun was still bright and warm, but they did not mind. They knew that Sam was happy too.

Lily was a very intelligent girl. She liked to learn new things and ask questions. She also liked to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom was making a cake and Lily wanted to help.

"Can I mix the batter, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey, but be careful. It's very sticky and messy," her mom said. She gave Lily a big spoon and a bowl.

Lily started to stir the batter with the spoon. She liked how it looked and smelled. She wondered how it would taste. She had an idea. She put down the spoon and picked up a fork.

"Mom, can I taste the batter with this fork?" Lily asked.

"No, honey, that's not a good idea. The batter has raw eggs and flour. It can make you sick. I recommend you wait until the cake is baked and cooled. Then you can have a slice," her mom said.

But Lily did not listen. She was too curious and hungry. She dipped the fork into the batter and put it in her mouth. She thought it would be yummy, but it was not. It was yucky and bitter. She made a face and spat it out.

"Yuck! This is gross!" Lily said.

She felt something in her throat. It was the fork. She had swallowed it by mistake. She started to choke and cough. She could not breathe. She felt scared and sorry.

"Mom, help me! I swallowed the fork!" Lily cried.

Her mom heard her and ran to her. She saw the fork sticking out of her mouth. She tried to pull it out, but it was too late. The fork had pierced her throat and made her bleed. She called 911, but it was no use. Lily was gone.

Her mom was very sad and angry. She wished she had stopped Lily from eating the batter. She wished Lily had listened to her recommendation. She wished Lily had been more careful and less intelligent.

One day, they want to make a big sun with glue and paper. They cut a big circle from yellow paper. They cut many rays from orange paper. They glue the rays to the circle. They glue the circle to the wall. They smile. They have a big sun.

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, you can't keep it. You have to take it off. Now. Or you will be in trouble."

One day, Sara and her mom go to the park to do yoga. They see a big tree with many leaves. They see a pond with ducks and fish. They see a bench with a heavy man sitting on it. The heavy man is reading a book and eating a sandwich.

Sara and her mom find a spot on the grass and start to do yoga. They stretch their arms and legs. They bend their backs and touch their toes. They balance on one foot and then the other.

The heavy man sees them and smiles. He puts down his book and sandwich and walks over to them. He says, "Hello, I like your yoga. Can I join you?"

Sara and her mom are surprised. They look at the heavy man and his big belly. They wonder if he can do yoga. They say, "Sure, you can join us. Yoga is for everyone."

The heavy man sits on the grass and tries to do yoga. He copies Sara and her mom. He stretches his arms and legs. He bends his back and touches his toes. He balances on one foot and then the other.

But the heavy man is not very good at yoga. He is too stiff and slow. He wobbles and falls. He grunts and groans. He makes funny noises and faces.

Sara and her mom try not to laugh. They help the heavy man get up. They say, "You did well. Yoga is hard at first. But if you do it more, you will get better and feel good."

The heavy man thanks them and says, "You are very kind. I like your yoga. I will do it more. Maybe next time I will be better."

Sara and her mom smile and say, "We hope to see you again. Yoga is more fun with friends."

They wave goodbye to the heavy man and go back to their yoga. They see the big tree, the pond, and the bench. They breathe slowly and make shapes with their body. They feel happy and calm.

Lily was a rabbit who loved to eat celery. She would hop around the garden and look for the green and crunchy sticks. She liked to share them with her friends, Ben and Rose, who were also rabbits.

One day, Lily found a big bunch of celery near the fence. She was very happy and wanted to show it to Ben and Rose. But when she got closer, she saw a big dog on the other side of the fence. The dog was barking and growling and showing his teeth. Lily was scared and ran away.

She found Ben and Rose and told them what she saw. "There is a big dog near the celery. He is very mean and loud. We can't go there," she said.

Ben and Rose looked at each other and then at Lily. They wanted to eat the celery, but they did not want to face the dog. They were worried and did not know what to do.

Then, they saw Sam, who was a mouse. Sam was very small, but he was also very brave. He heard Lily's story and said, "I can help you. I can sneak past the dog and get the celery for you. He won't see me or hear me. I am very fast and quiet."

Lily, Ben and Rose were surprised and grateful. They said, "Thank you, Sam. You are very kind and brave. But be careful. The dog is very big and scary."

Sam nodded and smiled. He said, "Don't worry. I will be back soon." He ran towards the fence and slipped under a hole. He saw the dog and the celery. He waited for the right moment and then dashed to the celery. He grabbed a stick and ran back to the hole. He did this several times until he had enough celery for everyone.

He brought the celery to Lily, Ben and Rose and said, "Here you go. Enjoy your snack. The dog did not notice me at all."

Lily, Ben and Rose were very happy and thanked Sam again. They ate the celery and shared some with Sam. They said, "You are our hero, Sam. You are very brave and smart. We are lucky to have you as our friend."

Sam blushed and said, "You are welcome. I am happy to help you. You are my friends too. And I like celery as well."

They all laughed and hugged. They learned that size does not matter, and that courage and kindness are more important. They also learned to appreciate their friends and their food. They lived happily in the garden and always looked out for each other.

"Uncle Bob, what is a lawyer?" she asked.

"A lawyer is someone who helps people with problems," he said.

"What kind of problems?" she asked.

"Sometimes people disagree or fight about things, like money or rules or rights. A lawyer tries to find a fair solution or speak for them in court," he said.

"What is court?" she asked.

"Court is a place where a judge and a jury decide who is right and who is wrong," he said.

"Who is a judge and a jury?" she asked.

"A judge is a person who knows the law and makes decisions. A jury is a group of people who listen to the lawyers and the witnesses and vote on the truth," he said.

"Who are the witnesses?" she asked.

"Witnesses are people who saw or heard something that is important for the case," he said.

Lily had many more questions, but then the phone rang. Uncle Bob had to answer it. It was a terrible call. He had to go to court right away. He had a very hard case. He had to defend a man who was accused of stealing a car.

"Can I come with you?" Lily asked.

"No, sweetie, court is not a place for children. It can be scary and boring. You stay here with your mom and play with your toys. I'll be back soon," he said.

He kissed Lily and her mom goodbye and ran out the door. Lily was sad. She wanted to see court and learn more about lawyers. She hoped Uncle Bob would win his case and come back happy. "Where is it?" Tom asks.

"I don't know!" Lily says.

The bird whistles again. It flies to the window and drops the piece on the floor. Tom and Lily are surprised. They run to the piece and pick it up. It is the frog's belly!

"Thank you, bird!" Tom says.

"Thank you, bird!" Lily says.

They put the piece in the puzzle. The puzzle is complete. The frog is smiling. Tom and Lily are smiling too. They clap their hands and whistle like the bird. The bird whistles back and flies away. Tom and Lily are happy. They hug each other and the puzzle. They love puzzles and birds.

Tom is a tall boy who likes to question everything. He always asks his mom and dad why the sky is blue, why the sun is hot, why the grass is green, and many other things. He wants to learn about the world and how it works.

One day, Tom sees that the leaves on the trees are changing color. Some are yellow, some are orange, some are red, and some are brown. He thinks they look pretty, but he wonders why they are different from before. He runs to his mom and asks her, "Mom, why are the leaves changing color?"

His mom smiles and hugs him. She says, "The leaves are changing color because the season is changing. Do you know what a season is?"

Tom shakes his head. He does not know what a season is.

His mom explains, "A season is a time of the year when the weather and the nature change. There are four seasons: spring, summer, fall, and winter. Right now, we are in fall. In fall, the weather gets cooler, the days get shorter, and the leaves change color and fall off the trees. Soon, it will be winter. In winter, the weather gets colder, the days get even shorter, and sometimes it snows. Do you like snow?"

Tom nods. He likes snow. He likes to make snowmen and snowballs and snow angels. He says, "I like winter. Winter is fun."

In summer, the weather gets hotter, the days get very long, and we can go to the beach and swim. Every season has something special and beautiful. Do you understand?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He says, "I think I understand. The seasons are different times of the year. They make the world change and look different. They are all nice in their own way."

His mom says, "That's right. You are a very smart boy, Tom. And you ask very good questions. I'm proud of you."

Tom smiles and hugs his mom. He says, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

They take the rod out of the water. It has a string and a hook at the end. They think it is a toy. They try to swing the rod and make the hook fly in the air. They laugh and have fun.

But then, the hook lands on a duck's wing. The duck is scared and hurt. It makes a loud noise. Quack, quack, quack! The other ducks are angry and scared too. They make loud noises too. Quack, quack, quack!

Tim and Lily are scared and sorry. They did not mean to hurt the duck. They drop the rod and run to the duck. They try to take the hook off the duck's wing. They say, "Sorry, duck. Sorry, sorry, sorry."

The duck is still loud and angry. It bites Tim's finger. Tim cries. Ouch, ouch, ouch! Lily cries too. She hugs Tim and says, "Sorry, Tim. Sorry, sorry, sorry."

A man comes to the pond. He is the owner of the rod. He is angry and sad. He says, "What are you doing with my rod? You hurt my duck. My duck is my friend. You are bad children. Go away, go away, go away."

Tim and Lily are very sad and ashamed. They say, "Sorry, man. Sorry, sorry, sorry." They run away from the pond. They go back to their mom. They tell her what happened. They say, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, sorry, sorry."

Mom is not angry. She is kind and understanding. She says, "It's okay, Tim and Lily. You made a mistake. You did not know. But you learned something today. You learned that a rod is not a toy. You learned that ducks are not toys. You learned that you have to be careful and gentle with animals. You learned that you have to say sorry when you hurt someone. You are good children. I love you, I love you, I love you."

Tim and Lily hug mom. They say, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, thank you, thank you." They feel better. They still love ducks. They still love the pond. But they will never play with a rod again.

Sara and Ben are best friends. They like to play in the park every day. They share their toys and snacks. They make a promise to always be nice to each other.

One day, Sara gets a new bike for her birthday. She is very happy. She wants to show Ben her bike. She calls him on the phone and says, "Come to the park, I have a surprise for you!"

Ben is excited. He runs to the park with his old bike. He sees Sara with her new bike. It is shiny and pink. It has a bell and a basket. Ben thinks it is very pretty. He says, "Wow, Sara, your bike is amazing! Can I try it?"

Sara says, "No, Ben, this is my bike. You have your own bike. You can't touch my bike. Go away!"

Ben is upset. He feels hurt and angry. He says, "But Sara, we are best friends. We share everything. You promised to be nice to me. Why are you mean to me?"

Sara says, "I don't care. This is my bike. I don't want to share it. I don't want to play with you. Go away!"

Ben is very upset. He cries and rides away. He thinks Sara is not his friend anymore. He thinks she broke their promise.

Sara feels bad. She sees Ben crying and riding away. She remembers their promise. She remembers how much fun they have together. She realizes she was mean to Ben. She wants to say sorry. She wants to share her bike. She wants to play with him.

She calls him on the phone and says, "Ben, please come back. I'm sorry. I was wrong. You can try my bike. I want to play with you. You are my best friend. Please come back."

Ben hears Sara's voice. He stops crying. He feels happy. He says, "OK, Sara, I'll come back. I'm sorry too. You are my best friend. I want to play with you."

He turns around and rides back to the park. He sees Sara waiting for him with a smile. They hug and say sorry. They share their bikes and play together. They keep their promise to always be nice to each other.

One day, Lily saw her dad working on his computer. He had many papers and pens and books on his desk. He typed and clicked and looked at the screen. Lily was curious. She wanted to help her dad too.

She climbed on a chair and reached for the computer. She saw many colors and shapes and letters on the screen. She pressed some buttons and moved the mouse. She heard some beeps and boops and noises. She thought she was mixing things on the computer.

But her dad was not happy. He saw what Lily was doing and shouted, "Lily, stop! You are messing up my work! You are not mixing, you are deleting and changing and closing!"

Lily was confused. She did not understand what her dad was saying. She did not know what deleting and changing and closing meant. She thought she was helping, not messing. She felt sad and scared.

She started to cry and ran to her mom. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. You did not mean to do anything wrong. You were just curious and wanted to learn. But you have to be careful with the computer. It is not a toy. It is a tool that your dad uses for his job. He needs it to do his work. You can help him by leaving it alone."

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, dad. I won't touch your computer again. Can I help you with something else?"

Her dad smiled and said, "I'm sorry too, Lily. I did not mean to yell at you. You are a good helper. How about you help me with this puzzle? It has many colors and shapes and letters too. But you can mix them and match them and make a picture."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, dad. I like puzzles. Let's mix and match and make a picture."

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with a hive. The hive has many bees. The bees make honey.

"Look, Lily, honey!" Tom says. "I am hungry. I want some honey."

"No, Tom, we cannot take the honey. The bees will be angry. They will sting us. It will hurt." Lily says.

"But I am very hungry. And honey is sweet. I have an idea. I will lie on the ground and pretend to sleep. You will shake the hive and run away. The bees will follow you. Then I will get some honey and eat it." Tom says.

"That is a bad idea, Tom. It is not nice to lie and steal. And it is not safe. The bees will find you and sting you. And I will be scared and alone. Please, do not do it." Lily says.

But Tom does not listen to Lily. He lies on the ground and closes his eyes. Lily shakes the hive and runs away. The bees come out and buzz. They see Lily and fly after her. They do not see Tom.

Tom opens his eyes and smiles. He sees the hive on the tree. He stands up and walks to the tree. He reaches for the hive. He thinks he is clever.

But he is not clever. He is silly. The hive is not empty. Some bees are still inside. They hear Tom and smell him. They are angry. They come out and sting Tom. Tom screams and cries. He drops the hive and runs away. He has no honey. He has only pain.

Lily hears Tom and comes back. She sees Tom and feels sorry for him. She helps him and hugs him. She says, "I told you, Tom. It was a bad idea. You should not lie and steal. You should be kind and careful. Next time, listen to me."

Tom says, "I am sorry, Lily. You are right. I was wrong. I will not lie and steal again. I will be kind and careful. Thank you for helping me. You are a good friend."

Lily and Tom go home. They have no honey. But they have each other. They are still hungry. But they are also happy.

"OK," the woman says. "Let's go!"

"OK, mom," Ben and Lily said. They nodded and moved away from the jellyfish. They decided to build a sandcastle instead. They used buckets and shovels and shells and seaweed. They had a lot of fun and forgot about the jellyfish.

The moral of the story is: Share and be kind. That is how you make friends and have fun.

Ben thinks. He remembers what his dad does when his car is sick. He has an idea.

"What were you thinking?" she asks them. "You know you are not supposed to go near the pond. It is dangerous. You could have drowned or got sick. You were very naughty and foolish."

She gives them a lecture about the rules and the risks of playing near the pond. She tells them they have to go home and change their clothes and drink some hot cocoa. She also tells them they are grounded and cannot play outside for a week.

Sara and Ben feel sorry and ashamed. They nod and say they are sorry. They promise to listen to their mom and never go near the pond again. They hope their mom will forgive them and love them. They also hope the pond will melt soon and they can play on the hill again.

They take the toy car to the park. They see a pond with ducks. The ducks are swimming and quacking. Tom and Sue think the ducks are funny. They want to drive the toy car near the pond.

But the toy car is too fast. It goes out of control. It bumps into a duck. The duck is scared and hurt. It makes a loud noise. Tom and Sue are scared too. They stop the toy car.

They run to the duck. They say sorry to the duck. They pet the duck gently. The duck feels better. It quacks softly. Tom and Sue feel better too. They give the duck some bread. The duck eats the bread. It is warm and happy.

Tom and Sue learn a lesson. They learn to be careful with their toys. They learn to be kind to animals. They drive the toy car away from the pond. They play with the ducks from a distance. They have fun and make new friends.

"It's mine!" Tom shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Jen yelled.

They pulled and tugged on the ball, but neither of them would let go. They started to fight and scream, making a lot of noise.

A fierce dog heard them and came running. He saw the ball and wanted it too. He barked and growled, showing his sharp teeth. He jumped on Tom and Jen, making them drop the ball. He grabbed it in his mouth and ran away.

Tom and Jen were scared and hurt. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had shared the ball instead of fighting over it.

A kind lady saw them and came to help. She had a band-aid and a cookie for each of them. She also had a small blue ball that she gave them.

"Here you go, children. This is for you to play with. But remember, sharing is caring. If you want to have fun, you have to settle your fights and be nice to each other. Fighting only leads to trouble. Do you understand?"

Tom and Jen nodded and said sorry to each other. They thanked the lady and took the blue ball. They decided to share it and play together. They learned their lesson and never fought over toys again.

As they were walking, Spot saw some new dogs playing in a park. Spot wanted to join in, but he was scared. His owner told him it was okay and encouraged him to go play. Spot was happy to have new friends and forgot all about the street.

Once upon a time, there was a big ocean with lots of fish and whales. A little boy named Timmy loved to play by the beach and watch the whales swim in the distant waters. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a cup of water to pour into the sand. Timmy loved to pour water, so he did it over and over again.

As Timmy was playing, he saw a big whale swimming towards the shore. The whale looked friendly, so Timmy waved at him. But the whale didn't stop swimming and soon he was very close to the beach. Timmy's mom saw the whale and told Timmy to run away, but Timmy was too scared to move.

Suddenly, the whale jumped out of the water and landed on the beach. Timmy was trapped under the whale and couldn't move. His mom tried to save him, but it was too late. Timmy was gone forever. From that day on, the people who lived by the beach never poured water into the sand again, because they knew the whales might mistake it for the ocean and come too close to shore.

Once upon a time, in a small wood, there lived a clumsy bear named Bobo. Bobo was not good at catching fish. He tried and tried, but he could not succeed. One day, a wise old owl saw Bobo and wanted to help him.

"Bobo," said the wise old owl, "you are too clumsy to catch fish like that. Let me show you a better way." The wise old owl showed Bobo how to catch fish by using a big stick. Bobo watched and listened very carefully.

"Good idea!" Lily said. "But we need a barrel first. Where can we find one?"

They looked around and saw a huge barrel near the fence. It was bigger than them and had a lid on top. They ran to the barrel and tried to lift it.

"It's too heavy!" Lily said, grunting.

"Maybe we can roll it!" Ben said, pushing the barrel. "Come on, help me!"

They pushed and pushed, but the barrel did not move. It was stuck in the mud.

"Oh no, what can we do?" Lily said, frowning.

"Maybe we can ask Dad for help!" Ben said, looking at the house. "He is strong and smart. He can help us move the barrel."

"OK, let's go and ask him!" Lily said, nodding.

They left the treasure on the dirt and ran to the house. They found Dad in the kitchen, making a sandwich.

"Dad, Dad, we need your help!" they said, jumping up and down.

"What is it, kids?" Dad said, smiling.

"We are playing pirates and we found a treasure, but we need a barrel to load it in, and there is a huge barrel in the backyard, but it's too heavy and stuck, and we can't move it, and we want to take it to our ship, and..." they said, talking very fast.

"Whoa, slow down!" Dad said, laughing. "You are playing pirates and you need a barrel, right?"

"Yes, yes, please help us!" they said, nodding.

"OK, OK, I'll help you. But first, finish your sandwich. You need some energy for your adventure." Dad said, cutting the sandwich in half and giving them each a piece.

"Thank you, Dad!" they said, taking the sandwich and eating it quickly.

"Are you ready?" Dad said, wiping their mouths.

"Yes, let's go!" they said, grabbing his hand and pulling him to the backyard.

They showed Dad the treasure and the barrel. Dad lifted the lid and looked inside.

"Hmm, this barrel is full of water. That's why it's so heavy and stuck." Dad said, shaking his head.

"Can you empty it, Dad?" Ben said, hoping.

"Sure, I can. But it might be a bit messy. Are you OK with that?" Dad said, smiling.

"Yes, yes, we don't mind!" they said, clapping.

"OK, then. Stand back and watch." Dad said, tipping the barrel over.

The water spilled out of the barrel, making a big splash and a puddle. The kids laughed and cheered.

"Wow, that was fun!" Lily said, jumping in the puddle.

"Now the barrel is empty and light. We can roll it to your ship." Dad said, standing the barrel up.

"Yay, thank you, Dad!" they said, hugging him.

They rolled the barrel to the box and put the treasure inside. They closed the lid and thanked Dad again.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun with your pirate game. But don't forget to clean up when you're done." Dad said, waving and going back to the house.

Anna thanked the lady and ran back to Ben. She hugged him and said. "It's okay, Ben. Mommy is coming. And a doctor too. They will fix your arm. I'm sorry the rope broke. I love you, Ben."

Ben hugged her back and said. "I love you too, Anna. You are a good sister. Thank you for getting help."

Tommy did not understand what Lily meant by pound. He did not know how to weigh things. He only knew how to count. He said, "But I can count, Lily. Look, there is a number on the cauliflower. "I don't know. Maybe someone forgot it," Lily said.

"Can we eat it?" Tom said. He was hungry.

Lily thought for a moment. She wanted to eat the melon too, but she was honest. She said, "No, we can't. It is not ours. We have to find the owner and give it back."

Tom was sad. He said, "But it looks so good. And no one is here. Maybe they don't want it anymore."

Lily shook her head. She said, "That is not fair. We have to be honest. Come on, let's look around and see if we can find the owner."

They took the melon and walked around the park. They asked everyone they met if the melon was theirs. But no one said yes. They were about to give up when they saw a man looking for something.

"Excuse me, sir. Is this your melon?" Lily asked.

The man looked surprised and happy. He said, "Yes, it is! Thank you so much for finding it. I left it here by mistake. I was going to have a picnic with my family. You are very kind and honest children. Here, you can have a slice of the melon as a reward."

Tom and Lily smiled. They were glad they did the right thing. They enjoyed the melon with the man and his family. It was sweet and juicy. They made new friends and had fun in the park.

Lily and Ben were playing with their dolls in the living room. They had a lot of fun dressing them up with different cloths and making them talk. Lily liked to display her dolls on the sofa, so everyone could see how pretty they were. Ben liked to make his dolls do funny things, like jumping and dancing.

"Look at my doll, Ben!" Lily said. "She has a pink cloth with flowers. She is very beautiful."

"Look at my doll, Lily!" Ben said. "He has a blue cloth with stars. He is very brave."

They smiled at each other and continued to play.

But then, Mom came into the living room. She looked troubled. She saw the cloths on the dolls and frowned.

"Lily, Ben, where did you get these cloths?" she asked.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They had taken the cloths from Mom's closet, when she was not looking. They thought she would not mind.

"Mom, we are sorry," Lily said. "We wanted to make our dolls look nice."

"Mom, we are sorry," Ben said. "We wanted to have fun with our dolls."

Mom sighed. She was not angry, but she was not happy either. She picked up the cloths and held them in her hands.

"These are not cloths for dolls, my dears," she said. "These are cloths for special occasions. They are very delicate and expensive. You should not play with them. You could damage them or lose them."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They did not know the cloths were special. They did not want to hurt Mom or the cloths.

"Mom, we are very sorry," they said together. "We did not know. We will not do it again."

Mom smiled. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I know you did not know, my dears," she said. "And I know you love your dolls. But you have to be careful with other people's things. You have to ask before you take them. And you have to respect them. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They said sorry again and gave Mom the dolls. Mom put the cloths back in her closet and gave them some other cloths to play with. They were not as pretty or as fancy, but they were still colorful and soft. Lily and Ben thanked Mom and went back to playing with their dolls. They were happy again. And Mom was happy too.

Tom and Lily were playing with their vehicles in the garden. Tom had a big red truck and Lily had a small yellow car. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving on the road.

"Beep beep! Out of my way!" Tom said, as he moved his truck closer to Lily's car.

"No, you move! This is my lane!" Lily said, as she tried to keep her car away from Tom's truck.

Tom did not listen. He wanted to have more space for his truck. He reached out and grabbed Lily's car from her hands. He threw it on the grass and laughed.

"Ha ha! Now I have two vehicles and you have none!" Tom said, as he drove his truck and Lily's car around the garden.

Lily was very sad and angry. She started to cry and ran to her mom, who was sitting on the porch.

"Mommy, Tom took my car and threw it away! He is mean!" Lily said, as she hugged her mom.

Mom looked at Tom and saw what he had done. She was not happy. She called Tom to come over.

"Tom, why did you take Lily's car and throw it away? That was not nice. You should share your toys and play nicely with your sister. How do you think she feels?" Mom said, as she scolded Tom.

Tom felt ashamed. He knew he had done something wrong. He looked at Lily and saw her tears. He felt sorry for her.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was selfish and rude. I should not have grabbed your car and thrown it away. Can I give it back to you and say sorry?" Tom said, as he walked to Lily and handed her car back to her.

Lily wiped her tears and smiled. She took her car and hugged Tom.

"Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. Can we play together again?" Lily said, as she held her car.

Tom nodded and smiled. He hugged Lily back.

"Yes, we can. I'm sorry for being mean. Can we be friends again?" Tom said, as he held his truck.

Lily and Tom went back to the garden and played with their vehicles. They made noises and pretended they were driving on the road. They shared their toys and played nicely with each other. Mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of them.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they saw a big package on the porch. It had a tag that said "To Mom and Dad, from Grandma and Grandpa". Tom and Lily were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Tom said.

But Tom did not listen. He ripped the tape and tore the paper. He saw a beautiful vase with flowers on it. He took it out of the package and held it in his hands.

"Wow, look at this! It's so pretty!" Tom said.

Lily was scared. She knew that the vase was very special and expensive. She tried to take it from Tom.

"Give it back, Tom! You're going to break it!" Lily said.

But Tom did not want to share. He pulled the vase away from Lily. They both tugged and pulled. The vase slipped from their hands and fell to the ground. It broke into many pieces. Tom and Lily gasped.

"Oh no! We destroyed the vase! Mom and Dad will be so sad and angry!" Lily said.

They heard the door open. It was Mom and Dad. They saw the broken vase and the dirty package. They were shocked and disappointed.

"What did you do, Tom and Lily? How could you be so naughty and careless? This vase was a gift from Grandma and Grandpa. They made it with love and care. It was very rare and precious. You ruined it!" Mom said.

Tom and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They knew they had done a bad thing. They cried and apologized.

"We're sorry, Mom and Dad. We were curious and selfish. We didn't mean to destroy the vase. We love you and Grandma and Grandpa. Please forgive us." Tom and Lily said.

Mom and Dad hugged them and said they forgave them. But they also said they had to learn from their mistake. They had to respect other people's things and not touch them without permission. They had to be careful and gentle with things that are fragile and beautiful. They had to be honest and responsible for their actions.

Tom and Lily nodded and said they understood. They promised to be better and more respectful. They helped Mom and Dad clean up the mess. They wrote a letter to Grandma and Grandpa to say they were sorry and that they loved them. They hoped they would not be too upset.

Lily and Tom are playing with their toy hammer and nails. They want to make a house for their dolls. Lily picks up a nail and tries to hit it with the hammer. But she is clumsy and misses the nail. She hits her finger instead. "Ow!" she cries. "That hurts!"

Tom hears her cry and runs to her. He sees her finger is red and sore. He feels sorry for her. He says, "Are you okay, Lily? Do you want a band-aid?" He shows her his box of band-aids. They have different colors and shapes.

Tom and Lily wanted to make a cake for Mom's birthday. They found a big bowl, some eggs, some flour and some sugar in the kitchen. They also saw a yellow stick on the table. It looked like cheese, but it was not cheese. It was butter.

"Let's put some butter in the cake," Tom said. "It will make it yummy."

"OK," Lily said. "But how do we get the butter out of the paper?"

Tom had an idea. He took the butter and put it in the microwave. He pressed some buttons and waited. He thought the microwave would make the butter soft and easy to use.

But he was wrong. The microwave made the butter very hot and melted. The paper around the butter caught fire. Smoke and flames came out of the microwave.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily shouted. They were very scared and worried.

Mom heard their cries and ran to the kitchen. She saw the fire and grabbed a wet towel. She opened the microwave and tried to wrap the towel around the burning butter. But it was too late. The fire had spread to the curtains and the wall. The kitchen was on fire.

Mom took Tom and Lily and ran out of the house. She called the firemen on her phone. They came with a big red truck and a loud siren. They sprayed water on the house and put out the fire.

But the house was ruined. The cake was ruined. Mom's birthday was ruined. Tom and Lily felt very sorry and sad. They hugged Mom and said they were sorry. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them. But she was also very angry and sad. She wished they had never touched the butter.

Tom and Amy start to organize their toys. They put the cars in the blue box and the dolls in the pink basket. They also put the blocks in the green bag and the books on the shelf. They work hard and fast. They want to make Mommy happy.

He found his nest and landed on it. He saw his friends. They were other birds who lived in the same tree. They saw his beak and his head. They were worried. They asked him what happened. Ben told them about the shiny thing. They said it was a bad thing. It was a trap. It was made by people. People sometimes put traps to catch birds. They said he was lucky to escape.

Ben felt sad and sorry. He wished he did not dive to the shiny thing. He wished he was more careful. He learned a lesson. He decided not to dive to unusual things anymore. He decided to dive only to things he knew. He was happy to have his nest and his friends. He thanked them for helping him. He rested in his nest and felt better. He still liked to dive, but he was smarter now.

Lily is faster than Tom. She runs and runs and runs. She is almost at the tree. She reaches out her hand to touch the number 10. But she does not see the big hole in the ground. She falls into the hole and hurts her leg. She cries and cries and cries.

"Hello, Tim and Jen. You are very kind and good. You gave me a nice meal. The bird was fat and tasty. I ate it and I am happy," the cat said.

Tim and Jen were very sad and angry. They cried and yelled at the cat. They threw rocks and sticks at the cat. But the cat did not care. It ran away and left Tim and Jen alone on the shore. They lost their friend and their nest. They felt bad and sorry. They wished they never met the bird and the cat. They wished they could restore the bird and the nest. But they could not. The end.

Ben and Mia were playing pirates in the garden. They had a big cardboard box that was their ship, and a stick that was their sword. They also had a hook that Mia's dad had given them. It was made of plastic, but it looked like a real hook.

"Arrr, matey, I'm the captain of this ship!" Ben said, putting the hook on his hand.

"No, I'm the captain, you're the first mate!" Mia said, waving her sword.

They pretended to fight, but they were really having fun. They made noises like cannons and waves and seagulls.

Suddenly, Ben felt a tickle in his nose. He tried to hold it in, but he couldn't. He sneezed very loudly, and the hook flew off his hand. It landed on a branch of a big tree.

"Oh no, my hook!" Ben cried.

"Look, it's up there!" Mia pointed.

They ran to the tree and looked up. The hook was hanging from the branch, but it was too high for them to reach.

"How can we get it back?" Ben asked.

Mia thought for a moment. She saw a rope that was tied to a swing. She had an idea.

"Maybe we can use the rope to get the hook!" she said.

She untied the rope from the swing and threw one end over the branch. She pulled the rope until it was close to the hook. She tied a knot on the rope and gave the other end to Ben.

"Pull the rope, Ben!" she said.

Ben pulled the rope hard. The hook moved a little, but it was stuck on the branch.

"Pull harder, Ben!" Mia said.

Ben pulled harder. The hook moved more, but it was still stuck.

"Pull harder, Ben!" Mia said again.

Ben pulled as hard as he could. The hook finally came off the branch, but it was so heavy that it pulled Ben down. He fell on the ground with a thud.

"Ouch!" Ben said.

Mia ran to him and helped him up. She saw the hook on the ground. She picked it up and gave it to Ben.

"Here's your hook, Ben. Are you okay?" she asked.

Ben rubbed his head. He smiled and took the hook.

"Thank you, Mia. I'm okay. You're a good pirate!" he said.

They hugged and laughed. They put the hook and the sword back in their box. They decided to play something else.

The end.

Little girl: "What's that, daddy?"

Her father: "That's an oyster, Sweetie. It's something special."

Little girl: "Can I have it?"

Her father: "No, Sweetheart. We can't take the oyster from the beach. That wouldn't be fair to the ocean. But you can look at it!"

Little girl: "Ok, daddy. But why can't I have it?"

Her father: "Because it's not fair to take things from the ocean. We should respect nature. Do you understand?"

Little girl: "Yes, daddy. I understand."

The little girl looked with admiration at the oyster, grateful that she was able to appreciate its beauty without taking it. She agreed that it wasn't fair to take things from nature. The little girl and her father left the beach with a newfound understanding of respect and fairness.

Lily played in the sand and built sandcastles with her dad. She saw some other kids in the water, having a great time. "I want to go in the water too!" Lily said.

Her dad said, "Sure, but don't spoil your fun by going too far out. Remember what Mom said about the tide."

Lily went in the water and had a great time splashing around. But then she started to go further and further out. Suddenly, a big wave came and Lily got scared. She remembered what her mom and dad said about the tide and quickly swam back to shore.

From that day on, Lily always listened to her parents and was careful around the tide. She learned that having fun is great, but it's important to be safe too.

Tom and Lily were scared. They ran to the house. The wolf ran after them. But the truck was in the way. The wolf tripped over the truck and fell. The blocks fell on the wolf. The wolf was hurt and angry. It howled and ran away.

Tom and Lily were safe. They hugged each other. They went back to the yard. They loaded the truck with more blocks. They drove it to the park. They had a yummy picnic. They were happy. They did not see the wolf again.

Lily loved to read novels. Novels were big books with many words and pictures. She liked to imagine she was in the stories with the characters. She had a white novel that was her favorite. It was about a princess and a dragon.

One day, Lily wanted to read her white novel, but she could not find it. She looked everywhere in her room, but it was not there. She felt sad and angry. She asked her mom, "Mom, where is my white novel? I want to read it!"

Mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but I gave your white novel to your cousin Jake. He was suffering from a cold and he was bored. I thought he would like to read it."

Lily was shocked. She said, "But Mom, that was my novel! I love it! You can't give it away!"

Mom said, "I know, Lily, but sharing is caring. Jake needed something to cheer him up. He will give it back to you when he feels better. Why don't you read another novel? You have many others."

Lily did not want to read another novel. She wanted her white novel. She felt like crying. She said, "No, Mom, I don't want another novel. I want my white novel. It's not fair!"

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily, I didn't mean to make you suffer. I know you love your white novel. But sometimes we have to be kind to others who are suffering too. Jake is your cousin and he loves you. He will take good care of your white novel and he will thank you for it. Can you be brave and patient, Lily?"

Lily thought about it. She did not like to see Jake suffer. He was her cousin and he loved her. Maybe he would enjoy her white novel and feel better. Maybe he would give it back to her soon. Maybe she could read another novel and find a new story to imagine. She said, "Okay, Mom, I will try. But I want my white novel back soon."

Mom smiled and said, "I'm proud of you, Lily. You are a good and generous girl. I'm sure Jake will appreciate your white novel and he will return it to you as soon as he can. Now, let's go and find another novel for you to read. Maybe we can find one with a fairy and a unicorn."

Lily nodded and followed Mom. She still missed her white novel, but she felt a little better. She hoped Jake would like her white novel and feel better too. She wondered what stories she would find in another novel. She liked to read novels. Novels were big books with many words and pictures.

Lily was scared. She did not like dark places. She also smelled something bad from the pipe.

"No, Ben, I don't want to go in the pipe. It is dark and smelly. Maybe there is a monster in there."

Ben laughed. He was not scared of anything. He wanted to have fun.

"Don't be silly, Lily. There is no monster in the pipe. It is just a pipe. Come on, it will be fun. I promise I will protect you."

He took Lily's hand and pulled her towards the pipe. Lily did not want to go, but she did not want to make Ben sad. She trusted him. He was her best friend.

They crawled into the pipe. It was dark and smelly. They could hear water dripping and rats squeaking. Lily was very scared. She held Ben's hand tightly.

"Ben, I don't like this. Can we go back, please?"

Ben looked around. He did not see any treasure. He only saw dirt and trash. He felt sorry for Lily. He saw that she was crying.

"Okay, Lily, we can go back. I'm sorry I made you come in the pipe. It was not fun. It was smelly and scary. You are very brave, Lily. I promise I will not make you do something you don't like again."

He hugged Lily and helped her out of the pipe. They ran back to the park. They played on the swings and the slide. They had fun. They were happy. They were friends. They kept their promises.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a whistle and a spin toy. The whistle makes a loud sound. The spin toy has many colors.

One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide. They want to try it. They take turns to go down the slide. They have fun.

But then, a mean boy comes. He sees their whistle and spin toy. He wants them. He says, "Give me your whistle and spin toy. They are mine now."

Tom and Mia are upset. They say, "No, they are ours. We got them from our moms. Go away."

The mean boy does not listen. He grabs their whistle and spin toy. He runs away. He laughs.

Tom and Mia cry. They want their whistle and spin toy back. They tell their moms what happened. Their moms are angry. They look for the mean boy. But they cannot find him. He is gone.

Tom and Mia are sad. They have no whistle and spin toy. They have no fun. They go home. They have a bad day.

Anna liked to write. She wrote on paper, on books, on walls, on anything she could find. She wrote her name, her numbers, her shapes, and her colors. She wrote with crayons, with pencils, with markers, and with chalk. She wrote every day, all the time, everywhere.

One day, Anna was writing on the tablecloth with a red crayon. She did not see her mom coming into the kitchen. She was too busy writing a big heart and a smiley face. She thought it looked pretty and fun.

"Anna, what are you doing?" her mom asked in a loud voice. She saw the red crayon and the tablecloth. She was angry and sad. She liked the tablecloth. It was white and clean. Now it was red and messy.

Anna looked up and saw her mom. She felt scared and sorry. She knew she did something bad. She dropped the crayon and hid her hands. She did not say anything.

"Anna, you know you are not supposed to write on the tablecloth. That is not nice. That is not good. You have to respect our things. You have to write on paper or on your board. Do you understand?" her mom said in a stern voice. She took the crayon and the tablecloth. She went to the sink to wash them.

Anna nodded. She understood. She felt ashamed. She did not want to make her mom angry and sad. She wanted to make her mom happy and proud. She wanted to say sorry and hug her mom. But she did not know how.

She went to her room and got her paper and her board. She wrote a big "I love you" and a big "I am sorry" on them. She drew a heart and a smiley face on them. She took them to the kitchen and gave them to her mom.

Her mom saw the paper and the board. She saw the words and the pictures. She smiled and hugged Anna. She said, "I love you too, Anna. And I forgive you. Thank you for saying sorry and for writing me these nice things. You are a good girl. You are a good writer. But please, only write on paper or on your board, OK?"

Anna smiled and hugged her mom back. She said, "OK, mom. I am sorry. I will only write on paper or on my board. I love you, mom. You are a good mom."

Her mom said, "You are welcome, Anna. I love you, too. You are a good daughter. Now, how about we have some dessert? I made some cookies for you. Do you want some?"

Anna said, "Yes, please, mom. I love cookies. They are yummy and sweet. Can I write on them with icing?"

Her mom laughed and said, "Sure, Anna. You can write on them with icing. But only on them, OK?"

Anna said, "OK, mom. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom."

They went to the table and ate some cookies. They wrote on them with icing. They wrote their names, their numbers, their shapes, and their colors. They had fun and they were happy. They forgot about the tablecloth and the crayon. They only remembered their love and their writing.

One day, Lily was very hungry and wanted some cream. She did not see mom anywhere. She thought mom was busy in another room. She decided to get some cream by herself. She climbed on a chair and opened the fridge. She saw a big jar of cream and reached for it. But she was too careless. She did not hold the jar well. The jar slipped from her hand and fell on the floor. The cream spilled everywhere. It made a big mess.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw Lily and the cream and the mess. She was very angry. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You were very naughty and careless. You did not listen to me. You made a big mess. You wasted the cream. You could have hurt yourself. You need to be punished."

Mom took Lily to her room and made her sit on the bed. She said, "You have to stay here for a while and think about what you did. You cannot play with your toys or watch TV. You have to say sorry and clean up the mess. And you cannot have any cream today."

Lily felt very sad and sorry. She did not like to be punished. She wished she had listened to mom. She wished she had not been careless. She wished she had not taken the cream. She said, "Mom, I am sorry. I will not do it again. I will clean up the mess. I will be good. Please forgive me."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I forgive you, Lily. I love you. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be careful and follow the rules. You have to respect the food and the fridge. You have to wait for me to give you cream. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I love you too. Thank you for forgiving me."

"This is the best apple ever!" Anna said.

Anna was surprised. She did not know what marry meant. She thought it was something nice.

"OK, Ben. I want to marry you. You are my best friend too." Anna said.

"Anna and Ben, you are too young to marry. But you can be friends forever. That is very important." Mama said.

"Yes, friends are very important. They share and care. They make you happy. They love you." Papa said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They understood. They loved their friends. They loved their parents. They were happy.

The end.

Moral value: Friendship is important and valuable. Friends share and care. Friends make you happy. Friends love you.

Inside the box, they saw many suits that were wild. They had bright colors, stripes, spots, and fur. They looked like animals. Tom and Sam wanted to match the suits with the hats and shoes. They took out the suits and put them on.

Tom put on a suit that looked like a tiger. He found a hat that looked like a tiger's head and shoes that looked like paws. He said, "Look at me, Sam! I am a wild tiger! Roar!"

Sam put on a suit that looked like a zebra. He found a hat that looked like a zebra's mane and shoes that looked like hoofs. He said, "Look at me, Tom! I am a wild zebra! Neigh!"

They ran around the attic, pretending to be wild animals. They had fun and made a lot of noise. They did not hear the door open and close. They did not see the man who came in.

The man was the owner of the box. He was a hunter who liked to hunt wild animals. He saw Tom and Sam in his suits. He thought they were real animals. He took out his gun and aimed at them.

Tom and Sam saw the man and his gun. They were very scared. They tried to run away, but it was too late. The man shot them and they fell down. They were not wild animals. They were just boys who liked to play dress up.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not yours. They may be dangerous.

"Let's make the puzzle!" said Bunny. He was good at hopping and finding things. He opened the box and poured out the pieces.

"Okay!" said Mouse. He was good at nibbling and fitting things. He picked up a piece and looked for another one that matched.

They worked hard on the puzzle. They made the edges first, then the middle. The puzzle showed a picture of a farm with many animals and plants.

"Look, there is a cow!" said Bunny, pointing to a black and white piece.

"And there is a carrot!" said Mouse, pointing to an orange piece.

They smiled and put the pieces together. They were happy and proud of their work.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was a dog, barking and running towards them. He wanted to play, but he did not see the puzzle.

"Watch out!" shouted Bunny. He grabbed Mouse and hopped away from the dog.

The dog ran over the puzzle and scattered the pieces. He did not mean to, but he ruined their work.

Bunny and Mouse looked at each other. They felt sorry for the dog. He was not a bad dog, just a clumsy dog.

"It's okay," said Bunny. He hopped back to the dog and patted his head.

Once upon a time there was a haveli with a big puddle outside. Everyone felt very uncomfortable because they had to step over the puddle. The haveli belonged to a kind and gentle family. They wanted everyone to feel welcomed and safe, so they decided to fix the puddle.

The father asked his son to help him. They brought a big bucket, filled it with dirt and stones, and emptied the bucket into the puddle. The son smiled as he watched the dirt and stones fill the puddle.

The father then asked his daughter for some help. She brought a broom and a big shovel. Together, the father and his daughter swept away the dirt and stones, until the puddle was gone. Then the daughter filled the empty space with sand and rock from the garden.

The family was so happy to have fixed the puddle. Now their visitors could come and feel comfortable. They celebrated with a big feast - everyone sure was happy!

The spider was very scared too, but he was clever. He shouted at the little girl, "Don't be afraid! I'm a brilliant spider and my webs help us catch bugs and keep us safe." The little girl was surprised. She listened to the spider and decided to leave the web in the garden. 

Soon, the little girl and the spider became friends. They would play together in the garden, and the spider reminded the little girl to never remove spider webs from the garden. They would have many happy days together, and the little girl loved her new brilliant spider friend.

Tim felt sad but still wanted to share the squash. He went to another friend, Lucy, and said, "Lucy, I have a big squash. Let's share it and have fun!" Lucy looked at the squash and said, "I don't like squash either, but thank you for being generous, Tim."

Tim felt very sad that no one wanted to share his squash. He decided to go home and eat the squash all by himself. As he sat down to eat, he thought about how he tried to value his friends by being generous. Suddenly, the squash rolled off the table and broke on the floor. Tim cried because he couldn't share the squash, and now he couldn't enjoy it himself. The squash was gone, and Tim felt very sad.

But then, the structure started to shake. Tim was scared now. He tried to go down, but it was too late. The structure fell down with a big boom. Tim was not okay, and everyone was sad. They knew that the structure was bad, but no one thought it would end like this.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They named him Frosty.

"Hello, Frosty!" Sara said. "You are our friend. We like you very much."

"Yes, we do!" Ben said. "You are the best snowman ever. Do you want to play with us?"

But Frosty did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot nose.

Sara and Ben did not know that Frosty had a secret. He had a magic hat that made him alive. But he could only talk when no one was around. He wanted to play with Sara and Ben, but he was afraid they would be scared.

One day, the sun was very bright and warm. Sara and Ben went inside to have lunch. Frosty felt the heat on his snow body. He started to melt.

"Oh no!" he said. "I have to find a cold place. Or I will be gone soon."

He looked around and saw a big house. He hoped there was a cold chamber inside. He took off his hat and put it on the snow. Then he rolled to the house.

He found a door that was open. He went inside and saw a lot of rooms. He looked for a chamber that was cold. He saw one with a sign that said "Freezer". He thought that was a good place.

He opened the door and went inside. He felt the cold air on his snow body. He was happy.

"Ah, this is better," he said. "I can stay here until the sun goes away."

He saw a lot of food in the freezer. He saw ice cream, popsicles, frozen peas, and more. He decided to make some friends.

"Hello, ice cream," he said. "You are cold like me. Do you want to talk?"

But the ice cream did not say anything. It just looked at him with a gentle face.

"Hello, popsicles," he said. "You are colorful like me. Do you want to play?"

But the popsicles did not say anything. They just smiled with their sticks.

"Hello, frozen peas," he said. "You are small like me. Do you want to have fun?"

But the frozen peas did not say anything. They just rolled with their bags.

Frosty felt sad. He missed Sara and Ben. He wished they could see him and hear him. He wished they could be his friends.

He put on his hat and hoped for a miracle.

Tom was very proud. He had caught an incredible crocodile. He went back to the water. He hoped to catch more fish. He liked to be a fisherman.

One day, she saw a rat in the garden. It was big and brown and had a long tail. Lily was scared of the rat. She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, there is a rat in the garden! It is ugly and mean!"

Mom came to the garden and looked for the rat. She did not see it. She said, "Lily, maybe it was not a rat. Maybe it was a squirrel or a rabbit. They are not ugly or mean. They are cute and shy."

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, mom, it was a rat. I know it was a rat. It had sharp teeth and red eyes. It made a loud noise. It was not cute or shy. It was bad and scary!"

Mom hugged Lily and said, "Lily, I believe you. But you know, not all rats are bad and scary. Some rats are nice and smart. They can learn tricks and help people. They can be friends with other animals. Maybe the rat in the garden was just looking for food or a home. Maybe it was afraid of you, too."

Lily thought about what mom said. She wondered if the rat was nice and smart. She wondered if it could learn tricks and help people. She wondered if it could be friends with other animals. She wondered if it was afraid of her, too.

She felt a little ashamed for calling the rat ugly and mean. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I was rude to the rat. Maybe it was not so bad. Maybe it was just lonely. Can we give it some food or a toy?"

Mom smiled and said, "That's very kind of you, Lily. Yes, we can give it some food or a toy. Maybe it will come back and say hello. Maybe it will be your friend. But remember, Lily, you have to be careful with rats. They can bite or scratch. They can carry germs or bugs. You have to wash your hands and stay away from their poop. You have to ask me or dad before you touch them. OK?"

Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. I will be careful with rats. I will wash my hands and stay away from their poop. I will ask you or dad before I touch them. But I hope the rat in the garden will like me. I hope it will be happy."

Mom kissed Lily and said, "I hope so, too, Lily. I hope it will be happy. And I hope you will be happy, too. You are a good girl, Lily. You are brave and curious and kind. I love you, Lily."

Lily hugged mom and said, "I love you, too, mom. You are the best mom in the world. Thank you for teaching me about rats. Thank you for being my friend."

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and animals. One day, they go to the park and see a big birdcage. Inside the birdcage, there are many colorful birds. They sing and fly and hop.

"Wow, look at the birds!" Anna says. "They are so pretty and playful. I want to touch them."

"No, Anna, we can't touch them," Ben says. "They belong to the park. They are happy in the birdcage. If we touch them, they might get scared or hurt."

But Anna does not listen to Ben. She wants to touch the birds. She climbs on the fence and reaches for the birdcage. She opens the door and puts her hand inside.

"Anna, stop!" Ben shouts. "You are doing a bad thing!"

But it is too late. The birds see Anna's hand and get scared. They flap their wings and peck at her. They make loud noises and fly out of the birdcage. Anna screams and lets go of the door. She falls off the fence and hurts her knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Anna cries. "The birds hurt me! They are mean!"

Ben runs to Anna and helps her up. He sees the blood on her knee and the feathers on her hand. He sees the empty birdcage and the birds flying away. He is sad and angry.

"Anna, you are silly and naughty," Ben says. "You did not number the birds. You did not care about them. You only cared about yourself. Now the birds are gone and you are hurt. You made a big mess."

Anna looks at Ben and feels sorry. She knows he is right. She did a bad thing. She wishes she listened to him. She wishes she could say sorry to the birds.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Anna says. "I'm sorry, birds. I was playful, but not in a good way. I learned my lesson. I will not touch the birds again. I will be nice and respectful."

But the birds do not hear Anna. They are far away. They are free and happy. They do not want to go back to the birdcage. They do not want to see Anna again.

The end.

Moral: Do not touch what is not yours. Respect the animals and their homes. Listen to your friends. Be playful, but not in a bad way.

Tom was a boy who liked to do things by himself. He was independent. He did not want to ask for help or share with others. He wanted to make his own toast for breakfast. He did not listen to his mom, who told him to be careful with the toaster.

He put two slices of bread in the toaster and pushed the lever down. He waited for the toast to pop up. He whistled a happy tune. He did not notice that the toaster was too hot and the bread was burning. He did not smell the smoke or hear the fire alarm.

Soon, the toast caught fire and the flames spread to the curtains. Tom was scared and ran out of the kitchen. He saw his mom and dad coming with a fire extinguisher. They put out the fire and hugged Tom. They were glad he was safe, but they were also angry and sad. They told him he was very naughty and careless. He could have hurt himself and the house. He had to learn to listen and ask for help when he needed it.

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He realized he was not as independent as he thought. He needed his mom and dad to teach him and protect him. He apologized and promised to be more careful and obedient. He also thanked them for saving him and the house. He learned that being independent does not mean being selfish or reckless. It means being responsible and respectful. He also learned that whistling is not a good idea when you are making toast.

Anna liked to draw on paper. She had many colors and shapes to make pictures. She drew flowers, animals, houses and people. She was very good at drawing and everyone liked her pictures.

One day, Anna went to school with her paper and colors. She wanted to show her friends her new picture. It was a big sun with a happy face and many rays. She thought it was very pretty and bright.

At school, she saw Ben. Ben was popular. He had many toys and games and he was good at running and jumping. He also liked to draw, but he only drew cars and planes. He thought they were cool and fast.

"Hi, Anna," Ben said. "What do you have there?"

Anna smiled and showed him her paper. "It is my sun. Do you like it?"

Ben looked at the paper and frowned. He did not like the sun. He thought it was silly and boring. He wanted to make fun of Anna.

"That is not a sun," he said. "That is a circle with a face. It is not real. My cars and planes are real. They can move and fly. Your sun can only stay on the paper. It is not fun."

Anna felt sad and angry. She did not like Ben's words. She liked her sun and she was proud of it. She wanted to answer Ben and tell him he was wrong.

She looked at her paper and had an idea. She took a yellow color and drew more rays around the sun. She made them long and sharp. She made them look like spikes.

She showed Ben her paper again. "This is my sun," she said. "It is real and it is fun. It can move and fly too. It can fly to your cars and planes and poke them with its rays. It can make them pop and crash. Then they will not be real or cool or fast anymore. They will be broken and gone. My sun is stronger and better than your cars and planes. Do you like it now?"

Ben was scared and surprised. He did not like Anna's sun. He thought it was mean and scary. He did not want it to poke his cars and planes. He did not want to make fun of Anna anymore.

He shook his head and ran away. He left his paper and colors behind. He did not want to draw anymore.

Anna smiled and picked up Ben's paper and colors. She liked them. She thought they were nice and useful. She decided to draw more pictures with them. She drew flowers, animals, houses and people. She also drew cars and planes. She made them look happy and friendly. She made them fly with her sun and have fun.

She showed her pictures to her friends. They liked them. They thought they were pretty and bright. They asked Anna to share her paper and colors. Anna said yes. She was happy and generous.

She was also very good at drawing and everyone liked her pictures. She was popular.

One day, Mia and Hoppy went to the park. They saw a big slide and a swing. Mia wanted to try them, but Hoppy was scared. He liked to stay on the grass and eat leaves.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" the boy screamed. "Get off me, you nasty bug!"

Mia got up and ran to Hoppy. She hugged him and thanked him.

"Look, Sara and Tom, this is a book about animals. You can learn their names and sounds. Can you say 'cat'?" Mom asks.

"Cat!" Sara and Tom say together. They point to a picture of a cat.

"Very good! And what does a cat say?" Mom asks.

"Meow!" Sara and Tom say. They make meowing sounds.

Mom smiles. She turns the page. "How about this one? What is this animal?"

Sara and Tom look at the picture. It is a yellow animal with black stripes and a long tail.

"Lion!" Sara says.

"No, no, Sara, that is not a lion. That is a tiger. A lion has a big mane. Can you say 'tiger'?" Mom says.

"Tiger!" Sara says.

"Tiger!" Tom says.

"And what does a tiger say?" Mom asks.

"Roar!" Sara and Tom say. They make roaring sounds.

Mom claps. She turns the page again. "You are doing great, Sara and Tom. Let's see one more animal. What is this one?"

Sara and Tom look at the picture. It is a green animal with a long neck and spots.

"Giraffe!" Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, that is a giraffe. Can you say 'giraffe'?" Mom says.

"Giraffe!" Sara says.

"Giraffe!" Tom says.

"And what does a giraffe say?" Mom asks.

Sara and Tom think. They do not know what a giraffe says.

"Moo?" Sara guesses.

"No, Sara, that is what a cow says. A giraffe does not say moo. A giraffe makes a low sound like this." Mom makes a low sound.

Sara and Tom try to make the same sound. They sound funny.

Mom laughs. She hugs Sara and Tom. "You are very smart, Sara and Tom. You learned a lot of animals today. Do you want a treat?"

"Ew!" Sara says.

"Yuck!" Tom says.

They spit out their apples. They look at Mom.

"Mom, these apples are not sweet and juicy. They are sour and bad." Sara says.

"Mom, why did you give us sour and bad apples?" Tom says.

Mom looks at the apples. She sees a sticker on them. It says "lemon".

"Oh, no, Sara and Tom, I am so sorry. I made a mistake. These are not apples. These are lemons. Lemons are sour and bad. They are not for eating. They are for making lemonade." Mom says.

Sara and Tom look at the lemons. They do not like lemons.

"Mom, can we have real apples, please?" Sara says.

"Mom, can we have something else, please?" Tom says.

"Banana!" Sara and Tom say.

"Mom, these bananas are good. Thank you, Mom." Sara says.

"Mom, we like bananas. Thank you, Mom." Tom says.

Mom smiles. She kisses Sara and Tom.

"You are welcome, Sara and Tom. I love you, Sara and Tom." Mom says.

"I love you, Mom." Sara and Tom say.

His mom sighed. She did not know what to do with Tommy. He was very stubborn. She said, "Tommy, you are being very rude. You have to eat what I give you. You cannot always have what you want. Soup is good for you and you have to eat it."

Tommy did not listen to his mom. He crossed his arms and pouted. He said, "No, no, no! I insist! I want bread and cheese and apples now!"
