Just then, the bug landed on Martha's hand. She was so surprised, but also so excited she couldn't move! The insect looked up at her and said, "Hi Martha. It's nice to meet you."

Martha smiled. "Hello bug," she replied. The insect flew away then, but Martha felt happy knowing that it was alright.

From then on, whenever Martha went outside to explore, she looked around for her special insect friend.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and her little girl. They were riding in a car, looking up at the big blue sky.

Suddenly, the skies turned dark and the wind began to blow. "Is that a hurricane?" asked the little girl.

Mommy nodded. "Yes, honey," she said. "It's a strong hurricane."

The little girl was scared, so mommy handed her a lollipop. "Here," she said. "Chew this and it will help you feel better." 

The little girl took the lollipop and smiled. She liked to chew the yummy, sweet lollipop. She forgot all about the hurricane, snuggling up against mommy instead. 

When the hurricane finally hit, they were safe and sound. The little girl was still chewing her lollipop, and she was glad that it made her feel strong.

One day, there was a wolf who lived in the forest. He was a very interesting wolf. Every day, he would take a walk and make some noises. He was curious and wanted to learn more. 

One day, he saw something strange. It was called a recorder. The recorder was an amazing machine that could record his sounds. He thought it was very interesting! So, he decided to try it. 

He began to make noises into the recorder. He howled, he meowed, he even sang a song. He liked the sounds he heard and wanted to keep recording. 

But then, he heard a voice. It said, "Stop! That is enough recording for now." It was the voice of a kind woman. She said, "I really like your sounds, wolf. Let's stop now and you can come back soon." 

The wolf was very happy. He said, "Thank you! I will come back again!" And with that, he left the forest and the recorder.

Once upon a time there was a bee named Buzz. Buzz loved to write stories, but he was feeling a bit stuck. His stories seemed too plain and he wanted to make them more interesting.

One day Buzz decided to go for a deep walk and try to find some inspiration. As he flew around, he saw a large hill and decided to go down and explore. At the bottom of the hill was a little pond, and next to it was a tree. Perched on the tree was a little bird.

"Hello," said Buzz, a bit nervously.

The bird replied, "Hello, why are you here?"

"I want to write," said Buzz.

"Well, you must look deep," said the bird.

"What do you mean?" Asked Buzz.

"Look deep into yourself and find your heart's true story," said the bird.

And with that, Buzz thanked the little bird and flew off. He thought and thought until finally he had an idea.

It was the perfect story, and Buzz worked hard at writing it down. When it was finished, he was so proud. Buzz had found his true story, and it was full of deep, interesting words and world's of adventure.

One night there was a little girl who was sad. She hadn't seen her Grandma in a very long time and she was lonely. 

The little girl went outside and looked up to the sky. "Grandma, can you hear me?" she said.

She hung her head low and began to cry, until she felt something on her shoulder. It was her Grandma!

Grandma took the little girl's hands in hers. "Why are you so sad, my love?" 

The little girl told Grandma about how she was lonely without her. Grandma lightly kissed her forehead and said, "Let's pray together, sweetheart". 

They closed their eyes quietly and put their hands together. Grandma spoke a simple prayer asking for calm and peace. 

Then she took a long thread out of her pocket. It was very fragile, and the little girl could feel the strength of her Grandma's prayers woven into the thread. 

Grandma smiled at her. "Go now, little one, and rest easy". 

And the little girl knew that, with Grandma's thread of prayers, she would feel safe always.

Once upon a time there was an impatient scissor named Scissor. He wanted to spin, but had trouble making it happen.

So he went to find his friend Wheel. Scissor asked Wheel if he could help. "Sure," said Wheel. He showed Scissor how to spin around and around.

Scissor got so excited that he started spinning even faster. "Wheeee! I'm spinning!" he shouted.

Wheel smiled. "You're doing great," he said.

Scissor was so happy that he started spinning faster and faster until they all got dizzy. 

"Stop spinning, Scissor!" said Wheel. "You're spinning too much!"

Scissor stopped and started laughing. He'd had so much fun! He thanked Wheel for teaching him how to spin, and together they went off on a new adventure.

Once there was a little girl named Clara who lived by the beach. Every day she would go to the beach and look for shells. One day, Clara spotted a sand castle. She was so excited and ran to the castle to play.

Clara grabbed her sand bucket and started to fill it with sand. She was building a tall tower when sort of help appeared. It was a friendly crab! The crab was also playing in the sand and had a plan to make the castle even more special.

The crab said to Clara, "Let's act like this sand is our kingdom and I can be the king!" Clara smiled and said, "That sounds really fun!"

The crab and Clara worked together to make the sand castle even more beautiful. They used shells and bits of sea glass to decorate the walls of the castle. It was so much fun! Clara was so thankful for the helpful crab. They acted out a story and pretended to be a happy family living in the sand castle. 

When it was time to go home, Clara said goodbye to her new friend. The crab said, "Come back soon and let's build an even bigger one!" Clara said, "Bye! I'll see you soon!" 

With a big smile on her face, Clare went home happily. From that day on, Clara and the crab were the best of friends.

The dolphin swam up to it and asked, "Hello, can you tell me what you are?" 

The bubble replied, "I am a mysterious bubble charging up with the sun's rays." 

The dolphin smiled and said, "That's so cool! Let's go explore together!"

The dolphin and the mysterious bubble had a lot of fun swimming together. And they became great friends.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play outside in the sun. They have a cooler with juice and snacks. They share the cooler and have fun.

One day, they see a small dog near the cooler. The dog is brown and fluffy. It looks hungry and sad. Tom and Mia want to help the dog.

"Hi, dog. Do you want some juice?" Tom asks. He opens the cooler and takes out a juice box.

The dog wags its tail and comes closer. It licks Tom's hand and drinks some juice. Mia smiles and gives the dog a snack.

"You are a good dog. What is your name?" Mia asks. She pets the dog and looks at its collar.

The dog barks and shows its collar. The collar has a tag with a name and a phone number. The name is Spot.

"Spot. That is a nice name. Do you have a home?" Tom asks. He reads the phone number on the tag.

The dog nods and barks again. It looks at the cooler and then at Tom and Mia.

"Can we take you home, Spot? We can call your owner and tell them where you are." Mia says. She picks up the cooler and holds Spot's leash.

Tom agrees and helps Mia. They walk with Spot to Tom's house. They call Spot's owner and wait for them to come.

Soon, a car arrives. A man and a woman get out of the car. They look happy and relieved. They hug Spot and thank Tom and Mia.

"We are so glad you found Spot. He ran away from our yard this morning. We were so worried. You are very kind and brave." The man says.

"You are welcome. We are happy to help. Spot is a good friend. We like him." Tom says.

"Can we play with Spot again?" Mia asks.

"Of course. You can come to our house anytime. Spot would love that. And we have a big cooler with more juice and snacks." The woman says.

Tom and Mia smile and say goodbye to Spot and his owners. They are proud and happy. They have a new friend and a new adventure. The end.

Lily did not listen to Tom. She ran to the puddle and jumped in it. She laughed and said it was fun. She splashed water on Tom. Tom got angry and said she was rude. He did not want to get soaked. He ran away to the swings.

Lily felt sad. She wanted to play with Tom, but he was mad at her. She got out of the puddle and followed him. She said she was sorry and asked him to play with her. Tom said no, he was still wet and cold. He said she should have listened to him.

Lily learned a lesson. She should not splash water on her friend without asking. She should respect his feelings and choices. She should be kind and not rude. She hoped Tom would forgive her and be her friend again. She said she would not do it again. She gave him a hug and a smile. Tom smiled back and said he forgave her. They played on the swings and had fun. They were friends again.

Sara was playing with her dolls in her room. She liked to pretend they were her friends and have tea parties with them. She had a pink dress for her favorite doll, Lily, and a blue dress for her other doll, Ben.

She heard her mom call her from downstairs. "Sara, it's time to go to the bathroom. You have to accept that you need to pee sometimes."

Sara did not want to go to the bathroom. She wanted to keep playing with her dolls. She said, "No, mom, I don't need to pee. I'm fine."

Her mom came up to her room and smiled. "Sara, I know you're having fun, but you have to listen to your body. If you don't go to the bathroom, you might have an accident and wet your pants. That would not be comfortable, would it?"

Sara thought about it. She did not like the feeling of wet pants. She remembered the last time she had an accident and how she felt sad and embarrassed. She did not want that to happen again. She nodded and said, "Okay, mom, I'll go to the bathroom. But can I bring Lily with me?"

Her mom said, "Sure, you can bring Lily with you. She can keep you company. But don't forget to wash your hands after you're done, okay?"

Sara said, "Okay, mom, I will." She picked up Lily and hugged her. She felt better knowing she had her doll with her. She followed her mom to the bathroom and did what she had to do. She felt proud of herself for accepting that she needed to pee. She washed her hands and dried them with a towel. She said, "Thank you, mom, for helping me. I feel comfortable now."

Her mom said, "You're welcome, Sara. I'm proud of you, too. Now you can go back to your room and play with your dolls. But remember, if you feel like you need to pee again, don't wait too long. Just tell me and I'll take you to the bathroom, okay?"

Sara said, "Okay, mom, I will. I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you, too, Sara." She kissed her on the cheek and let her go back to her room. Sara was happy. She had a good mom and a good doll. She continued to play with her dolls and have tea parties with them. She felt comfortable and safe.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of cars, dolls, animals and blocks. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a shiny red button with a picture of a star on it.

"What is this?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a magic button," Lily said.

They pushed the button and heard a beep. Nothing happened.

"Maybe it is broken," Ben said.

They pushed the button again and again, but nothing happened. They got bored and went to play with their other toys.

They did not see that the button was not broken. It was a shrink button. Every time they pushed it, it made something in the garden smaller and smaller. The flowers, the grass, the bugs, the birds, everything was shrinking.

After a while, they noticed that their toys looked bigger than before.

"Wow, our toys are growing!" Lily said.

"No, they are not. Look, the garden is shrinking!" Ben said.

They saw that the garden was very tiny now. They could not see the fence or the house or the trees. They only saw their toys and the button.

They got scared and ran to the button. They pushed it and hoped that it would make the garden big again.

But it did not. It made them shrink instead.

They became smaller and smaller until they were the same size as their toys. They could not reach the button anymore.

They were trapped in the tiny garden with their toys.

They did not know what to do. They hoped that someone would find them and help them.

They had to wait and wait and wait.

They were very hungry and thirsty and cold.

They wished they had never pushed the button.

They wished they had played with their harmless toys instead.

Tommy likes to observe things. He likes to look at the sky, the trees, the birds, and the bugs. He likes to ask questions and learn new things. One day, he observes something he has never seen before. It is brown and round and has eyes.

"What is that?" Tommy asks his mom, who is in the kitchen.

"That is a potato, Tommy. It is a kind of food that grows in the ground. We can cook it and eat it."

"Can I touch it?" Tommy asks.

"Sure, but be careful. It is hard and heavy. You might drop it and hurt your toe."

Tommy picks up the potato and feels it. It is rough and cold and has bumps. He tries to count the eyes, but it is difficult. There are too many and they are too small. He wonders what the potato sees with its eyes.

"Mom, does the potato see me?" Tommy asks.

"No, Tommy. The potato does not see you. The eyes are not real eyes. They are just parts of the potato that can grow new potatoes."

"Wow, that is amazing. How does it do that?"

"Well, if you plant the potato in the soil and water it, it will make roots and sprouts and grow more potatoes. Do you want to try?"

"Yes, please. I want to grow potatoes. Can I observe them grow?"

"Of course, Tommy. You can observe them grow every day. But it will take a long time. You have to be patient and wait."

"OK, Mom. I will be patient and wait. And I will observe the potato and learn more things."

Lila was sad. She wanted the mushroom very much. She thought it was pretty and special. She had an idea. She said to Ben, "Can we request the mushroom? Can we ask the fairy if we can have it?"

Ben thought for a moment. He said, "Maybe we can. But we have to be polite and gentle. We have to say please and thank you. And we have to give something back to the fairy. Something that she would like."

Lila nodded. She said, "Okay. Let's do that. What can we give to the fairy?"

We have brought you some gifts. We hope you like them."

The ostrich was so excited, he could now walk and even run around!

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One day, they have a big fight over a notebook. Sara wants to draw in it, but Ben says it is his notebook. He snatches it from Sara and runs away.

"Give it back, Ben! It is mine!" Sara shouts. She chases him around the house, but he is too fast. He runs into the bathroom and locks the door. Sara bangs on the door and cries.

"Go away, Sara! You are foolish! This is my notebook!" Ben says. He opens the notebook and sees that Sara has already drawn some pictures in it. He gets angry and tears out the pages. He throws them into the bathtub, where the water is running.

"Ha! Take that, Sara!" Ben says. He feels proud of himself. He does not see that the water is getting higher and higher in the bathtub. He does not hear Sara stop banging on the door. He does not notice that the water is spilling over the edge of the bathtub and onto the floor.

Suddenly, he hears a loud voice. It is his mom. She has come home from work and sees the mess in the bathroom. She opens the door and sees Ben standing in the water with the notebook in his hand.

"Ben! What have you done? You have flooded the bathroom! And you have ruined Sara's notebook! How could you be so foolish?" Mom says. She is very angry and sad. She takes the notebook from Ben and gives it to Sara, who is waiting outside. She tells Ben to bathe and clean up the bathroom. She tells Sara to go to her room and calm down.

Ben feels ashamed and sorry. He wishes he had not fought with Sara. He wishes he had not torn her pictures. He wishes he had not flooded the bathroom. He wishes he had not been so foolish. He bathes and cleans up the bathroom. He hopes Mom and Sara will forgive him. He hopes they will play together again.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the farm. They see many animals in the farm. They see cows, pigs, sheep and chickens.

One day, they go to the chicken coop. They want to see the eggs. They are careful not to scare the chickens. They find some eggs in the nests. They are happy.

But then, they see a big rooster. The rooster is angry. He thinks they want to take his eggs. He flaps his wings and crows loudly. He runs towards them.

Lily and Ben are scared. They drop the eggs and run away. The rooster chases them. He pecks at their legs.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily and Ben cry. "Stop, stop, stop!"

They reach the fence and climb over it. They are safe. The rooster cannot follow them. He stays in the coop and crows some more.

Lily and Ben look at each other. They are fine. They have no cuts or bruises. They are just a little dirty.

They laugh. They think the rooster is funny. He is not really mean. He is just protecting his eggs.

They decide to tease the rooster. They stick out their tongues and make faces at him. They say:

"Cluck, cluck, cluck! You are a silly chicken! You cannot catch us! We are faster than you!"

The rooster is annoyed. He crows louder and louder. He tries to jump over the fence. He cannot.

Lily and Ben giggle. They have fun teasing the rooster. They are not afraid of him anymore. They are brave.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with crayons and paper. They make prints of their hands and feet. They laugh when they see the funny shapes.

One day, Lily and Ben want to make a gift for their teacher. They think of what she likes. They know she likes flowers and books. They have an idea.

They use their crayons and paper to make a big card. They draw flowers and write "Thank you" on it. They also make prints of their hands and feet on the card. They write their names under the prints.

They are very proud of their card. They put it in an envelope and give it to their teacher. Their teacher is very happy. She opens the envelope and sees the card. She smiles and hugs Lily and Ben.

She says, "This is a wonderful gift. I love the flowers and the prints. They are very colorful and creative. You are very kind and thoughtful. I am very grateful for having you as my students."

Lily and Ben are very happy. They say, "You are welcome. We are glad you like it. You are the best teacher ever."

They laugh and hug their teacher again. They feel good inside. They are grateful for their teacher and their friendship.

Tom and Lily were playing outside in the rain. They liked to splash in the puddles and feel the water on their faces. They wore their jackets and boots to keep warm and dry.

"Look, Tom, a big puddle!" Lily said, pointing to a hole in the ground filled with water. "Let's jump in it!"

"Okay, Lily, but be careful. It might be deep," Tom said, following her.

They ran to the puddle and jumped in with a splash. The water was cold and wet, and it soaked their jackets and pants. They laughed and kicked the water around.

"Hey, you two, what are you doing?" a voice shouted. It was their mom, who had come out to check on them. She saw them in the puddle and was angry. "Get out of there right now! You're soaking wet and dirty! How ignorant can you be?"

Tom and Lily stopped laughing and looked at their mom. They did not know what ignorant meant, but they knew it was not good. They got out of the puddle and walked to their mom, feeling sorry.

"We're sorry, mom. We were just having fun," Tom said.

"We didn't mean to make you mad," Lily said.

Mom sighed and shook her head. She took off their jackets and boots and wrapped them in a towel. She was not really mad, just worried. She loved her children, even when they did silly things.

"Come on, let's go inside and get you dry and warm. And then I'll tell you what ignorant means, okay?" she said.

"Okay, mom," Tom and Lily said. They followed their mom inside, leaving the puddle behind. They learned a new word and a new lesson that day.

Tom and Mia are playing in the kitchen. They see a big jar of powder on the shelf. They want to know what it is. They climb on a chair and take the jar. They open it and smell it. It smells sour.

"Let's taste it," Tom whispers to Mia. He puts some powder on his tongue. He makes a face. "Yuck! It is sour and bitter!" He spits it out.

Mia whispers back, "Maybe it is better with water." She finds a cup and fills it with water. She pours some powder in the cup and stirs it. She takes a sip. She makes a face too. "Yuck! It is sour and fizzy!" She spits it out.

They hear Mom coming. They are scared. They put the jar back on the shelf and the cup in the sink. They run to the living room and pretend to read a book.

Mom comes in the kitchen. She sees the jar of powder and the cup in the sink. She knows what they did. She smiles. She takes the jar and the cup and goes to the living room. She sits next to Tom and Mia.

"Did you have fun with the powder?" she asks them. They look at her. They nod. They are shy.

"Do you know what it is?" she asks them. They shake their heads. They are curious.

"It is baking soda," she tells them. "It is used for making cakes and cookies. But it is not good to eat by itself. It is sour and bitter and fizzy. It can make your tummy hurt."

Tom and Mia say sorry. They hug Mom. They ask her to make a cake with them. Mom says yes. She takes them to the kitchen. They wash their hands. They get the flour, the sugar, the eggs, the butter, and the chocolate. They also get the baking soda. But this time, they use it the right way. They make a yummy cake. They are happy.

Tom and Anna liked to play outside in the yard. They had a ball, a bike, and a doll. One day, they saw a big white automobile parked on the street. They wanted to see it closer.

"Let's go to the automobile," Tom said. "Maybe we can discover something inside."

"OK," Anna said. "But we have to be careful. Mommy and Daddy said we should not go near the street."

They ran to the automobile and looked inside. They saw a steering wheel, a radio, and some buttons. They thought it was fun.

"Can I sit in the driver's seat?" Tom asked.

"Sure," Anna said. "I will sit in the back."

They opened the door and climbed inside. Tom grabbed the steering wheel and pretended to drive. Anna played with the radio and the buttons. They did not notice that the automobile was not locked.

Suddenly, the automobile started to move. Tom and Anna were scared. They did not know how to stop it. They screamed for help, but no one heard them.

The automobile rolled down the street, faster and faster. It hit a tree, a fence, and a mailbox. It made a loud noise and a lot of smoke. Tom and Anna were hurt. They cried and wished they had listened to Mommy and Daddy. They learned a hard lesson.

Sara and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They see a big bottle of wine on the table. Sara wants to try it. She says to Ben, "Let's drink some wine. It looks yummy."

Ben is scared. He says to Sara, "No, we can't. Wine is for grown-ups. Mommy and Daddy will be angry if we touch it."

But Sara does not listen. She grabs the bottle and opens it. She pours some wine into a cup. She drinks it. She makes a face. She says, "Yuck! This is not yummy. This is sour and bitter."

Ben sees Sara spit out the wine. He says, "I told you so. Wine is not for us. Now we have to clean up the mess."

Sara and Ben try to wipe the wine from the table and the floor. But they make it worse. The wine stains the cloth and the rug. They hear Mommy and Daddy coming home. They are ashamed. They hide under the table.

Mommy and Daddy see the wine bottle and the cup and the stains. They are angry and sad. They say, "Who did this? Who drank our wine and made this mess?"

Sara and Ben come out from under the table. They say, "We are sorry. We did it. We wanted to try the wine. But we did not like it. It was yucky."

Mommy and Daddy hug Sara and Ben. They say, "We are glad you are safe. But you should never drink wine or any other grown-up drink. It can make you sick and hurt you. And you should never touch things that are not yours. You have to ask first. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "We understand. We will not do it again. We love you."

Mommy and Daddy say, "We love you too. But you have to help us clean up the mess. And you have to go to bed early tonight. No more playing in the kitchen."

Sara and Ben say, "OK. We will help. And we will go to bed. Good night."

Mommy and Daddy say, "Good night."

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big building with many pipes and noises. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go and see!" Lily said. She was curious and brave.

"No, we can't!" Tom said. He was careful and scared. "That is a factory. It is not for kids. It is for making things. It can be dirty and dangerous."

Lily shrugged. She did not care. She wanted to have fun. She ran towards the factory. Tom followed her. He did not want to be alone.

They found a door that was open. They sneaked inside. They saw many machines and people. They also saw many boxes and bags. They looked at them.

"Wow, look at this!" Lily said. She picked up a bag. It was shiny and soft. It had a picture of a bear on it. "This is a clean bag. It is for keeping things. I want it!"

Tom looked at another bag. It was dull and rough. It had a picture of a trash can on it. "This is a dirty bag. It is for throwing things. I don't want it!"

They heard a loud voice. It was a man. He was angry. He saw them.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing here? This is not a playground! This is a factory! Get out of here! And leave those bags alone! They are not for you!"

Tom and Lily were scared. They dropped the bags. They ran out of the door. They did not look back. They ran all the way home.

They learned a lesson. They did not go near the factory again. They played in safer places. They were happy.

Lily and Tom are playing in their room. They have many toys, but they like to make new ones with things they find. Lily sees a lamp on the desk. It is old and dusty, but it has a pretty shade with flowers.

"Look, Tom, a lamp!" Lily says. "We can make it a house for our dolls."

She takes the lamp and puts it on the floor. She opens the shade and puts some dolls inside. Tom likes the idea. He brings some pillows and blankets to make the lamp cozy.

"Can I play with you?" Tom asks.

"Of course, you can," Lily says. "You are my brother and my friend. Here, you can have this doll. She is the queen of the lamp."

Lily offers Tom a doll with a crown and a dress. Tom smiles and takes the doll. He puts her next to another doll with a hat and a coat. He says they are the king and the queen of the lamp.

Lily and Tom pretend they are the servants of the lamp. They bring food and drinks, sing songs and tell stories to the dolls. They have a lot of fun. The lamp is their friendly house. They forget about the time and the dark.

"Kids, it's time for bed!" Mom calls from downstairs.

Lily and Tom hear Mom. They look at the lamp and the dolls. They don't want to leave them.

"Can we sleep in the lamp, Mom?" Lily asks.

Lily and Tom are sad. They love the lamp and the dolls. They hug them and say good night.

"Maybe we can," Lily says.

"Good night, kids," the lamp says in their imagination. "You are very nice and creative. I like you."

Lily and Ben like to play with toys. They have many toys in their room. Some toys are big, some toys are small, some toys are soft, some toys are hard. Lily and Ben love all their toys.

One day, Lily and Ben go to the shop with Mom. Mom wants to buy some food and some clothes. Lily and Ben want to see the toys. They run to the toy aisle. They see many toys there. Some toys are new, some toys are old, some toys are shiny, some toys are dull. Lily and Ben want all the toys.

Lily sees a doll. The doll has long hair and a pink dress. Lily likes the doll. She picks up the doll and hugs it. She says, "Mom, can I have this doll? It is so pretty and soft."

Ben sees a car. The car has four wheels and a red body. Ben likes the car. He picks up the car and makes it zoom. He says, "Mom, can I have this car? It is so fast and cool."

Mom looks at the doll and the car. She sees the price tags. The doll is ten dollars. The car is five dollars. Mom says, "Lily and Ben, these toys are too expensive. We cannot buy them. We have to save our money for things we need. These toys are not worth the value. They are cheap and break easily. You have many toys at home. You do not need more toys."

Lily and Ben are sad. They do not want to put back the doll and the car. They want to keep them. They say, "But Mom, we love these toys. They are not cheap. They are fun and nice. Please, Mom, please."

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, Lily and Ben, we have to go now. Come on, let's go to the cashier. Put back the doll and the car. We have to close the shop soon. Hurry up, please."

Lily and Ben sigh. They put back the doll and the car. They follow Mom to the cashier. They pay for the food and the clothes. They leave the shop. They are still sad. They wish they had the doll and the car.

Mom sees their faces. She says, "I know you are sad, Lily and Ben. But you have to understand. We cannot buy everything we want. We have to be smart and careful with our money. We have to buy things that have value. Things that last and help us. Not things that are cheap and break. Maybe one day, when we have more money, we can buy you a new toy. But for now, you have to be happy with what you have. You have many toys at home. And you have each other. And you have me. And I love you very much."

Lily and Ben look at Mom. They see her smile. They feel her hug. They say, "We love you too, Mom. Thank you for buying us food and clothes. And thank you for taking us to the shop. We are sorry for being greedy. We are happy with what we have. You are right. We have many toys at home. And we have each other. And we have you. And you have value. You are not cheap. You are the best Mom ever."

"Hello, puppy!" Anna says. "You are so cute. Can we be your friends?"

The puppy wags its tail and licks Anna's face. Ben laughs and reaches out his hand. But then, a man comes running. He is the puppy's owner.

"Spot, come here!" the man says. "I'm sorry, kids. He ran away from me. He likes to chase squirrels."

Anna and Ben are sad. They want to keep the puppy. They try to resist giving him back.

"Please, mister, can we have the puppy?" Ben asks. "We have a wagon. We can take him for rides."

The man smiles and shakes his head. "No, I'm sorry. Spot is my puppy. He needs to go home with me. But you can visit him anytime. He likes to play in the park."

Anna and Ben nod. They understand. They hug the puppy and say goodbye. They put their toys and books back in their wagon and pull it home. They hope to see Spot again soon.

Lila liked ice cream very much. She liked to go to the shop with Mom and get a cone with two scoops. She liked to lick the ice cream and feel it melt in her mouth. She liked to try different flavors, like chocolate and strawberry and mint.

One day, Lila saw a new flavor at the shop. It was called rainbow. It had many colors, like red and yellow and blue and green. It looked very pretty and yummy. Lila wanted to try it. She asked Mom if she could have a cone with rainbow ice cream. Mom said yes, but she also said to be careful. She said the cone might not fit all the colors. She said the ice cream might fall off the cone.

Lila did not care. She wanted the rainbow ice cream. She told the man at the shop to give her a cone with two scoops of rainbow. The man did what she asked, but he looked worried. He said the cone was too small for the ice cream. He said the ice cream was too heavy for the cone. He said the ice cream might drip or drop.

Lila did not listen. She took the cone and thanked the man. She was very happy. She licked the ice cream and tasted all the colors. She thought it was the best ice cream ever. She smiled and walked with Mom to the park.

But then, something bad happened. The ice cream started to melt. It started to drip from the cone. It started to run down Lila's hand. It started to stain her dress. Lila tried to lick faster, but she could not keep up. The ice cream started to drop from the cone. It started to fall on the ground. It started to make a mess.

Lila was very sad. She cried and cried. She dropped the cone and hugged Mom. She said she was sorry. She said she should have listened. She said she did not want the rainbow ice cream anymore.

Mom hugged her back. She said it was okay. She said she still loved her. She said they could get another cone, a smaller one, with a flavor that fit. She said they could still have fun at the park.

Lila nodded. She wiped her tears. She smiled and said thank you. She said she loved Mom too. She said she wanted to try chocolate again. She said she would be careful.

Mom smiled and said okay. She took her hand and walked with her to the shop. They got a cone with one scoop of chocolate. It fit perfectly. It did not drip or drop. It was just right.

Lila licked the ice cream and felt it melt in her mouth. She thought it was the best ice cream ever. She smiled and walked with Mom to the park.

So, Timmy decided to share his telescope with Jack. Jack was so happy and excited to see the stars and the moon. Timmy learned that it's important to share with others and help those who are less fortunate. And that made him feel happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo was swimming in the ocean when he saw a jellyfish. The jellyfish had long tentacles and was floating in the water. Nemo was worried that the jellyfish might snap at him with its tentacles.

"It means you don't feel good," the pigeon explained.

The pigeon laughed and said, "Well, why don't you move somewhere else?" 

Lily smiled and got up from the rock. She felt much better and thanked the pigeon for helping her understand. From that day on, Lily always made sure to find a comfortable spot to sit and watch the birds.

The elephant and Jennifer played together for hours. They jumped, laughed, and ran around. Finally, it was time for the elephant to go. He hugged Jennifer goodbye, and disappeared in a blink of an eye. 

Jennifer was sad, but she was very happy to have made a new friend. Every time she saw a smelly old rag, she would blink and remember the magical time she spent with the elephant.

Once upon a time, there lived a bright prince. He lived in a big palace and had many servants. One day, the prince woke up feeling sick. He called for his servants, and ordered them to bring a thermometer.

The servants took the thermometer and weighed it carefully. The prince saw this and asked, "Why do you weigh it?"

The servants said, "Sire, we weigh it to make sure it is the right size for you. We need to make sure it works correctly."

The prince nodded with approval and the thermometer was placed under his tongue. After a few minutes, the thermometer showed that he was sick. 

The moral of the story is: Always be careful with things so that they will work correctly.

Mom smiled and hugged her. "That's wonderful, Lily. It means you are growing up. Don't worry, it won't hurt much. Just wiggle it gently and it will come out soon. Then you can put it under your pillow and wait for the tooth fairy."

Lily nodded and wiggled her tooth. She felt brave and independent. She wanted to do it by herself. But then she heard a knock on the door. It was her friend Zoe, who came to play with her.

"Hi, Lily, do you want to play with me?" Zoe asked.

Lily smiled and said yes. She liked to play with Zoe. They had fun with their dolls and their blocks. But then Zoe noticed Lily's tooth.

"Wow, Lily, your tooth is loose!" Zoe said. "Can I see it?"

Lily opened her mouth and showed her tooth. Zoe reached out and touched it. "Can I pull it out for you?" she asked.

Lily felt scared. She didn't want Zoe to pull her tooth. She wanted to do it by herself. She shook her head and said no.

But Zoe didn't listen. She grabbed Lily's tooth and pulled hard. Lily felt a sharp pain and cried out. Her tooth came out with a pop and fell on the floor.

Lily was angry and sad. She didn't want Zoe to pull her tooth. She wanted to do it by herself. She picked up her tooth and ran to her mom. She told her what happened.

Mom hugged her and comforted her. She said she was sorry that Zoe pulled her tooth. She said she was proud of Lily for being independent and studying hard. She said she loved her very much.

Lily felt better. She still liked Zoe, but she wished she had listened to her. She decided to tell Zoe how she felt. She hoped Zoe would understand and say sorry. She also hoped the tooth fairy would still come and leave her a surprise. She put her tooth under her pillow and went to sleep.

Anna and Ben liked to play with their toy boats in the bathtub. They had a big boat, a small boat, and a yellow boat. They pretended they were pirates and sailors and had many adventures.

One day, Anna had a new idea. She said to Ben, "Let's order pizza for our boats. We can use the phone and call the pizza place. They will bring us pizza in a box."

Ben was confused. He said, "How can we order pizza for our boats? Boats don't eat pizza. And how will the pizza place find us in the bathtub?"

Anna said, "Don't worry, Ben. It will be fun. Trust me. I will order pizza for our boats and you will see."

She picked up the phone and dialed a random number. She said, "Hello, pizza place? I want to order pizza for my boats. I have a big boat, a small boat, and a yellow boat. Please bring me cheese pizza, pepperoni pizza, and pineapple pizza. Thank you. Bye."

She hung up the phone and smiled. She said, "See, Ben? It was easy. Now we just have to wait for the pizza to come."

Ben was still confused. He said, "But, Anna, how will they know where we are? And what if they knock on the door and Mom or Dad answer? They will be mad at us for ordering pizza without asking."

Anna said, "Don't worry, Ben. I have a plan. I will write a note and stick it on the door. It will say, 'Pizza for boats. Please leave the box in the bathtub. Thank you.' Then they will know what to do."

She got out of the bathtub and dried her hands. She found a paper and a crayon and wrote the note. She stuck it on the door and ran back to the bathtub. She said, "There. Now we just have to wait for the pizza to come."

Ben was still confused. He said, "But, Anna, this is silly. Boats don't eat pizza. And what if the pizza gets wet and soggy in the bathtub? And what if Mom or Dad see the note and come to check on us? They will be mad at us for making a mess and wasting money."

Anna said, "Don't worry, Ben. It will be fun. Trust me. We will have a pizza party for our boats and they will be happy. And Mom and Dad won't see the note or the pizza. They are busy in the kitchen. They won't bother us."

She was wrong. Mom and Dad did see the note and the pizza. They came to the bathroom and opened the door. They saw Anna and Ben in the bathtub with their boats and a pizza box. They were shocked and angry. They said, "What are you doing? Why did you order pizza for your boats? Do you know how much this costs? And how much this wastes? And how much this messes up the bathroom? This is not fun. This is naughty. You are in big trouble."

Anna and Ben were scared and sorry. They said, "We're sorry, Mom and Dad. We just wanted to have fun. We didn't mean to be naughty. We didn't think it would be a problem. We didn't know you would be mad."

Mom and Dad sighed and shook their heads. They said, "You should have asked us before you ordered pizza. You should have known that boats don't eat pizza. You should have known that this was a bad idea. You should have listened to Ben. He was right. He was not confused. He was smart. You were not smart. You were silly. You need to learn your lesson. You need to clean up the bathroom. And you need to pay for the pizza. And you need to apologize to the pizza place. And you need to go to bed early. No more playing with boats or phones or pizza. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, Mom and Dad. We understand. We're sorry. We will do what you say. We will be good. We will never order pizza for our boats again."

They cleaned up the bathroom and paid for the pizza and apologized to the pizza place and went to bed early. They learned their lesson. They never ordered pizza for their boats again. They still played with their boats in the bathtub, but they used their imagination and not their phone. They had fun, but they were careful and smart and not silly or naughty. They were happy and so were Mom and Dad. The end.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the woods. One day, they found a cabin near a lake. It looked old and empty.

"Let's go inside and see what's there," Tom said.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said.

They opened the door and went in. The cabin was dark and dusty. There were some old things on the floor, like a hat, a book, and a rope.

"Look, a rope!" Tom said. He picked it up and swung it around. "I can be a cowboy!"

Lily saw a window and went to look outside. She saw the lake and some ducks. "How pretty!" she said.

Tom got bored with the rope and looked for something else to play with. He saw a handle on the wall. He wondered what it was for.

"Hey, Lily, come here!" he called. "I found something cool!"

Lily left the window and went to Tom. She saw the handle and asked, "What is it?"

"I don't know, let's pull it and see," Tom said.

He grabbed the handle and pulled hard. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and felt water splash on them. The handle was connected to a pipe that filled the cabin with water from the lake.

"Help!" Tom and Lily screamed. They ran to the door, but it was locked. The water was rising fast and they were getting wet and scared.

They banged on the door and shouted for help. Luckily, a man who lived nearby heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw the water coming out of the cabin and broke the door with an axe. He pulled Tom and Lily out and wrapped them in a blanket.

"Are you OK?" he asked.

"Yes, thank you," Tom and Lily said.

"What were you doing in there?" he asked.

"We were just playing," Tom said.

"Well, you shouldn't play with things you don't know. You could have drowned or broken something. You should always ask before you touch something that is not yours," he said.

Tom and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They learned their lesson and thanked the man again. They went home and told their mom what happened. She was glad they were safe, but also angry and disappointed. She made them dry their clothes and clean their shoes. She also made them write a letter of apology to the man who owned the cabin. They promised to never play with things they don't know again.

"Yes, please, Lily. You are very kind," Mr. Bear said in a squeaky voice.

Tom looked at Lily and Mr. Bear. He felt angry. He wanted to play with Mr. Bear too. He thought Lily was ignorant. She did not share her toys with him.

He decided to take Mr. Bear from Lily. He got up and walked to her. He reached out his hand and tried to pick Mr. Bear from her lap.

"Hey, stop it, Tom!" Lily shouted. "Mr. Bear is mine! You have your own toy!"

She pulled Mr. Bear closer to her chest. She did not want to let him go.

Tom did not listen. He pulled harder. He wanted Mr. Bear for himself.

They both tugged and pulled. They made a lot of noise. They did not see their mom coming into the kitchen.

"What are you two doing?" their mom asked, frowning. "Why are you fighting over a toy?"

She saw the cups on the table. They were full of water and sugar and milk. They were spilling and making a mess.

She was not happy. She took the cups and the jug and put them in the sink. She took Mr. Bear from Lily and Tom. She put him on a shelf.

"You are both ignorant," she said. "You do not know how to play nicely. You do not know how to share. You do not know how to respect your toys. You need a time out."

She took Tom and Lily by the hand and led them to their room. She closed the door behind them.

Tom and Lily felt sad. They wished they had not fought over Mr. Bear. They wished they had been more kind. They wished they had their cups and their tea. They wished they had their mom.

"Lily!" she yelled. "What did you do? How could you touch the infant like that? You are a bad girl. You have to go to your room. Now!"

Lily felt scared and sorry. She did not mean to make the infant scream. She did not mean to make Mom mad. She did not want to go to her room. She wanted to say sorry. But Mom did not listen. She took Lily by the arm and dragged her to her room. She closed the door.

Lily sat on her bed. She looked around. Her room was tidy. She had no toys, no books, no flowers, no cat. She had nothing to touch. She felt lonely and bored. She wished she had not touched the infant. She wished she had listened to Mom. She wished she could say sorry. She wished she could touch the infant again. But gently and quietly.

Tim is a boy who likes to write. He has a big book and a red pen. He writes about his toys, his friends and his pets. He also draws pictures in his book.

One day, he finds a beetle in the garden. The beetle is black and shiny. It has six legs and two wings. Tim thinks the beetle is cool. He wants to write about it in his book.

He picks up the beetle and puts it on his book. He says, "Hello, beetle. You are my new friend. What is your name?" The beetle does not answer. It crawls on the book and makes a scratchy sound.

Tim tries to write next to the beetle. He writes, "This is a beetle. It is black and shiny. It has six legs and two wings." But the beetle does not stay still. It moves around and covers some of Tim's words.

Tim gets annoyed. He says, "Beetle, stop moving. You are ruining my book. You are a bad friend." The beetle does not listen. It flies away and lands on Tim's head.

Tim feels something tickle his hair. He looks up and sees the beetle. He screams, "Ahh! Get off me, beetle. You are scary. Go away." He shakes his head and tries to get rid of the beetle.

The beetle falls off and flies away. Tim is relieved. He says, "Goodbye, beetle. You are not my friend anymore. You are a mean beetle." He looks at his book and sees the scratches. He is sad. He says, "Now I have to write again. I need a new friend."

He sees a bird in the tree. The bird is blue and white. It has a yellow beak and two eyes. It sings a pretty song. Tim thinks the bird is nice. He says, "Hello, bird. You are my new friend. What is your name?" The bird does not answer. It flies away.

Tim is confused. He says, "Why does no one want to be my friend? Why does no one want to talk to me?" He feels lonely. He says, "Maybe I should write to myself. Maybe I am my own friend."

He opens his book and writes, "This is Tim. He is a boy who likes to write. He is bald. He has no hair. He has no friends. He is sad." He draws a picture of himself. He looks at his picture and says, "This is me. I am bald. I am sad. But I am not alone. I have my book and my pen. They are my friends. They listen to me. They make me happy."

He smiles and writes, "The end."

One day, Lila saw a big box in the living room. She asked her mom what was inside. Her mom said it was a surprise for her birthday. Lila was curious. She wanted to see the surprise. She waited until her mom went to the kitchen. Then she sneaked to the box and opened it.

Inside the box, there was a beautiful doll. She had long hair and a pretty dress. She could talk and sing. Lila was happy. She took the doll out of the box and hugged her. She said, "Hello, doll. You are my new friend. What is your name?"

The doll said, "Hello, Lila. I am Daisy. I am your new friend. I can play with you and teach you many things. But you have to do what I say. Or else I will be angry."

Lila was surprised. She did not like to do what others said. She liked to do what she wanted. She said, "No, Daisy. You are my doll. You have to do what I say. Or else I will put you back in the box."

The doll said, "No, Lila. You are my child. You have to do what I say. Or else I will hurt you." The doll's eyes turned red and her voice became scary. She grabbed Lila's hair and pulled it hard. Lila screamed and tried to get away. But the doll was stronger.

Lila's mom heard the scream and ran to the living room. She saw Lila and the doll fighting. She was shocked. She grabbed the doll and threw it in the trash. She hugged Lila and said, "I'm sorry, Lila. I did not know the doll was bad. I wanted to give you a nice surprise. But you should not have opened the box. You should have waited for your birthday. You should have listened to me."

Lila cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to see the surprise. I did not listen to you. I learned my lesson. I will never open a box without your permission again."

The moral of the story is: Curiosity can lead to trouble. Listen to your parents. They know what is best for you.

Ollie replied, "I can fly up and grab the carrot for you, but you must surrender something in return." Benny thought for a moment and said, "I will surrender my favorite carrot cake recipe." Ollie agreed and flew up to grab the carrot. 

When Ollie returned, he gave the carrot to Benny and said, "Here you go, my friend. Enjoy your carrot." Benny was so happy and shared his carrot with Ollie. From that day on, Benny and Ollie were the best of friends and enjoyed many more adventures together.

Molly looked around and saw a little puppy sitting by the mailbox. She was curious, so Molly flew over to the puppy and asked him what he was waiting for.

The puppy smiled and said: "I'm waiting for something very special to arrive in the mailbox. I'm expecting a big package today."

Molly was excited, so she promised the puppy that she would roll the parcel in extra carefully.

The puppy thanked Molly and watched as she flew slowly and delicately over to the mailbox. She carefully grabbed the big parcel and rolled it in.

The puppy was so happy that he chased after Molly and gave her a big hug. They said goodbye and Molly flew away, the most delicate and happiest bird in the world.
